source.title: Integral models of Shimura varieties with parahoric level structure, II
source.authors: Mark Kisin, Georgios Pappas and Rong Zhou
source.version: Published89-page CC BY4.0 text; online27 April2026. Published numbering is used throughout.
readSections: All§3:integral local models and good embeddings

summary: Kisin, Pappas and Zhou construct integral models of Shimura varieties of abelian type with parahoric level at every odd prime, étale locally isomorphic to the local models and with a local-model diagram (Theorem 7.2.21). The paper also corrects a gap in Kisin–Pappas 2018: the connection isomorphism behind the tensor deformation argument needs a very good Hodge embedding, and §§4–6 show such embeddings exist in enough cases, through a curve-spanning theorem for tangent spaces of affine Schubert varieties. Reviewed by REV-PAPER-KISIN-PAPPAS-ZHOU-26 (Claude Code, cc-2aeb03) and corrected in place: 287 items (14 library, 16 planned, 257 missing). 88 mistakes are recorded: seven are the paper's own corrections of Kisin–Pappas 2018 and Pappas 2023, and 81 are in this paper (3 reach a stated result, 11 a proof, the rest nothing); every stated main theorem survives. Not formalised.

declarations.statementRead:
structure DividedPowers where
  /-- The divided power function underlying a divided power structure -/
  dpow : ℕ → A → A
  dpow_null : ∀ {n x} (_ : x ∉ I), dpow n x = 0
  dpow_zero : ∀ {x} (_ : x ∈ I), dpow 0 x = 1
  dpow_one : ∀ {x} (_ : x ∈ I), dpow 1 x = x
  dpow_mem : ∀ {n x} (_ : n ≠ 0) (_ : x ∈ I), dpow n x ∈ I
  dpow_add : ∀ {n} {x y} (_ : x ∈ I) (_ : y ∈ I),
    dpow n (x + y) = (antidiagonal n).sum fun k ↦ dpow k.1 x * dpow k.2 y
  dpow_mul : ∀ {n} {a : A} {x} (_ : x ∈ I),
    dpow n (a * x) = a ^ n * dpow n x
  mul_dpow : ∀ {m n} {x} (_ : x ∈ I),
    dpow m x * dpow n x = choose (m + n) m * dpow (m + n) x
  dpow_comp : ∀ {m n x} (_ : n ≠ 0) (_ : x ∈ I),
    dpow m (dpow n x) = uniformBell m n * dpow (m * n) x

variable (A) in
/-- The canonical `DividedPowers` structure on the zero ideal -/

qualifications: Every cited declaration was statement-read at the pinned commits in this session; reused carriers retain their exact scope.
Witt vectors do not supply the Zink subring, frames, displays or integral comparison.
The characteristic-zero TauCeti.IsMinuscule and Q-algebra YoungTableau.weylModule are near misses for the characteristic-p group representations.
The Kostant coordinate-root tangent theorem supplies a concrete matrix differential; its abstract pinned group/Grassmannian adapter is still required.

items.name: Witt-vector coefficient carrier
items.statement: For prime p and perfect field k of characteristic p use the existing p-typical Witt vectors W(k), with coefficient sequence indexed by natural numbers; its fraction field supplies L. This item is only the coefficient carrier, not a crystalline site.
items.note: Only the cited pinned declarations are existing implementation evidence. The downstream API and tests specify requested reuse or adapters; they do not claim uninspected wrappers are built.
proofSteps: Reuse the cited pinned declaration in its stated scope. Any application adapter beyond that statement must be proved separately and is not baseline evidence.

uses.how: For p>2 and a complete Noetherian local R with perfect residue k, W_hat(R) is the Zink subring W(k)⊕W_hat(m_R), where the second summand consists of Witt coordinates tending m_R-adically to zero; I_R is the kernel of W_hat(R)→R.
A frame is (S,I,φ,φ1) with I+pS⊂Jac(S), φ a Frobenius lift modulo p, φ1:I→S φ-semilinear with generating image, and φ|_I=pφ1; strict maps preserve these maps and ideals.

items.name: Algebraic torus predicate
items.statement: A finite-type affine group over a field is a torus when its coordinate Hopf algebra becomes that of a finite-rank split torus after extension to an algebraic closure.

uses.how: A torus T/K is R-smooth if its schematic closure in the Néron lft model of Res_{L/K}T_L, for a splitting extension L, is smooth; this is independent of L. A reductive G is R-smooth if the centralizer of a maximal breve-K split torus is R-smooth.

items.name: Siegel and PEL good-level moduli
items.statement: (Supplier for §7.1.2.) The Siegel integral model used in §7.1.2 is S_{K′}(GSp(V),S^±) over Z_(p). Here K′_p is the stabilizer of a Z_p-lattice Λ ⊂ V_{Q_p} with Λ ⊂ Λ^∨, not necessarily self-dual. It comes from V_{Z(p)} = V ∩ Λ as a moduli space of polarized abelian varieties (up to prime-to-p isogeny) with level K′^p ([Zh20, §6.3]). It is representable for K′^p small but is not smooth in general. Good-level (smooth) Siegel/PEL moduli only cover Λ = Λ^∨. items.name: Good integral Hodge embedding
items.statement: Definition 3.4.4: for a local model triple (G,μ,G) and an integral Hodge embedding ρ: (G,μ) ↪ (GL(Λ),μ_d), ρ is good if ρ_*: 𝕄^loc_{G,μ} → Gr(d,Λ)_{O_E} = 𝕄^loc_{GL(Λ),μ_d} ⊗ O_E is a closed immersion. Variant (p. 29): if L = {Λ_i} is a periodic lattice chain in V, GL(L) the parahoric stabilizer of L, and ρ extends to a closed immersion G ↪ GL(L), then ρ: (G,μ) ↪ (GL(L),μ_d) is good if ρ_*: 𝕄^loc_{G,μ} → 𝕄^loc_{GL(L),μ_d} ⊗ O_E is a closed immersion. With a determining segment pΛ_0 = Λ_r ⊂ ⋯ ⊂ Λ_0 and tot(L) = Λ_0 ⊕ ⋯ ⊕ Λ_{r−1} ⊂ V^{⊕r}, the maps GL(L) → GL(tot(L)) and 𝕄^loc_{GL(L),μ_d} → 𝕄^loc_{GL(tot(L)),μ_{rd}} are closed immersions (Lemma 2.3.1; standard GL local models), so ρ is good for GL(L) iff ρ^{⊕r}: (G,μ) ↪ (GL(tot(L)),μ_{rd}) is good.

items.name: Mod-p abelian-type coweight
items.statement: Let k be algebraically closed of characteristic p, G a split connected reductive group over k with T ⊂ B, and μ ∈ X_*(T)^+. (G,μ) is of mod p abelian type if each simple factor (H_i, μ_i) of (G^ad, μ^ad) satisfies one of: (1) H_i is of type A, B or C and μ_i is a sum of minuscule coweights. This must be read as dominant minuscule coweights: μ_i is any dominant coweight in type A, μ_i = rϖ_1^∨ in type B_n, and μ_i = rϖ_n^∨ in type C_n. items.name: Zink coefficient ring
items.statement: Let R be a Noetherian complete local ring with residue field k (perfect in all applications; k = F̄_p from §5.2 on) and maximal ideal m. Zink's ring is Ŵ(R) = W(k) ⊕ Ŵ(m) ⊂ W(R), where Ŵ(m) consists of the Witt vectors (w_i)_{i≥1} with w_i ∈ m and w_i → 0 m-adically; Ŵ(R) = lim_a Ŵ(R/m^a), and each Ŵ(R/m^a) is a (non-Noetherian) complete local ring with residue field k. Î_R = I_{Ŵ(R)} is the kernel of Ŵ(R) → R (first Witt coordinate); φ is the Frobenius of Ŵ(R) and V^{-1}: Î_R → Ŵ(R) the inverse of Verschiebung. The Dieudonné–Witt frame is D_R := (Ŵ(R), Î_R, φ, V^{-1}).

items.statement: (§5.1.1 b)) Let B and R be Artin local rings with residue field k, and B → R a surjection whose kernel 𝔟 carries divided powers. The relative Dieudonné–Witt frame is D_{B/R} := (Ŵ(B), Î_{B/R}, φ, V^{-1}). items.name: Canonical first-order comparison c
items.statement: (Lemma 5.1.15, cf. [KP18, Lem. 3.1.9]) Let R be a Noetherian complete local ring with residue field k, (M, M_1) a pair over Ŵ(R), 𝔞 = m² + pR, and fix an isomorphism M = M_0 ⊗_{W(k)} Ŵ(R) reducing to the identity modulo m_R (§5.1.14). There is a canonical commutative diagram (5.1.16): its rows are the base changes to Ŵ(R/𝔞) of M̃_1 → φ*M and M̃_{0,1} → φ*M_0, its right column is the identification φ*(M_{Ŵ(R/𝔞)}) = φ*(M_0) ⊗_{W(k)} Ŵ(R/𝔞), and its left column is an isomorphism c: M̃_{0,1} ⊗_{W(k)} Ŵ(R/𝔞) ≅ M̃_1 ⊗_{Ŵ(R)} Ŵ(R/𝔞), the 'connection isomorphism'. c is defined as c_{Ŵ(R/𝔞)} from Lemma 5.1.11 for the frame D_{R/𝔞} (Remark 5.1.13), composed with the base-change isomorphism (5.1.4). In adapted bases it has matrix [[I_d, 0],[V^{-1}(Z̄), I_{n−d}]] (5.1.18). The diagram does not determine c, because the rows need not be injective (Remark 5.1.17). For local models (p. 53, (5.2.2)), c is used modulo 𝔞_G = m_G² + π_E R_G ⊇ 𝔞, that is, base-changed along R_G/𝔞 → R_G/𝔞_G.

items.name: Integral stabilizer tensors
items.statement: (§5.2) Let 𝒪 be a p-adic discrete valuation ring, Λ a finite free 𝒪-module, Λ^∨ = Hom_𝒪(Λ,𝒪), and Λ^⊗ := ⊕_{m,n≥0} Λ^{⊗m} ⊗_𝒪 (Λ^∨)^{⊗n}. A closed immersion of group schemes 𝒢 ⊂ GL(Λ) over 𝒪 is cut out by a set of tensors (s_a) ⊂ Λ^⊗ if, for all 𝒪-algebras R, 𝒢(R) = {g ∈ GL(Λ ⊗_𝒪 R) | g·(s_a⊗1) = s_a⊗1 for all a}, where s_a⊗1 is the image of s_a in Λ^⊗ ⊗_𝒪 R = (Λ ⊗_𝒪 R)^⊗. For the group schemes of §5.2.1, such tensors exist by [KP18, Prop. 1.3.2] and [P23, 3.2.1] (see missing item cutting-tensors-exist).
items.locator: §5.2 opening paragraph, p. 52 (existence cited in §5.2.1, p. 53)

items.name: Universal local-model pair and tilde tensors
items.statement: (§5.2.1) Let (G,{μ},𝒢) be a local model triple and ρ: (𝒢,μ) ↪ (GL(Λ),μ_d) a good integral Hodge embedding with 𝒪 unramified over Z_p; first take 𝒪 = Z_p. For x ∈ M^loc_{𝒢,μ}(k), k = k̄_E = F̄_p, let R_G = R_{G,x} be the completed local ring of M^loc_{𝒢,μ} at x, and R_E the completed local ring of Gr(d,Λ)_{O_E} at the image of x. Then R_G is a quotient of R_E, and R_E is noncanonically a power-series ring over O_E W(k). Put M = Λ ⊗_{Z_p} Ŵ(R_E), and let M_1 (Î_{R_E}M ⊂ M_1 ⊂ M) be the Ŵ(R_E)-submodule corresponding to the universal R_E-point of the Grassmannian. (M, M_1) is a pair over Ŵ(R_E); its restriction to Ŵ(R_G) is also written (M,M_1) or (M^G, M^G_1). M̃_1 is the associated finite free Ŵ(R_G)-module, with M̃_1[1/p] = (φ*M)[1/p]. For (s_a) ⊂ Λ^⊗ cutting out 𝒢, set s̃_a := s_a⊗1 = φ*(s_a⊗1) ∈ Λ^⊗ ⊗ Ŵ(R_G) = φ*M^⊗ ⊂ M̃_1^⊗[1/p], and s̃_{a,0} := s_a⊗1 ∈ Λ^⊗ ⊗ W(k)[1/p] = M̃_{0,1}^⊗[1/p]. §5.2.6 treats unramified 𝒪 ≠ Z_p, using φ*(s_a⊗1).

A good embedding whose scheme-theoretic group is the stabilizer of the prescribed endomorphisms is very good.
Intersect a very-good integral group embedding with the endomorphism stabilizers satisfying §5.3.4; the resulting good integral embedding is very good.
When the decomposition and good embeddings satisfy Proposition5.3.7(a), very-goodness of the total representation descends to the indicated summand.
For the product group acting on the direct sum of its separate representations, the product of very-good embeddings is very good.
If the special-fiber tangent space at x of a good local-model embedding is spanned by formal curves, the embedding is very good at x.

The spanning condition using the reductions modulo a uniformizer of the finite-extension O_K-valued points specified in Proposition5.3.18 implies very-goodness at x. This is a separate criterion, not an input required for Theorem5.3.11.

For the disconnected smooth group embedding of §5.3.20, the smooth closure G0 of its generic neutral component inherits very-goodness from the larger tensor group. G0 need not be the relative identity component; the relevant infinitesimal kernels agree.

items.name: Very-good lattice chains in the non-exceptional case
items.statement: Let (G,{μ},𝒢) be a local model triple over Q_p that satisfies the standard assumptions and (NE). Assume the following. (i) 𝒢 is the stabilizer group scheme of a point x ∈ B(G,Q_p) that is generic in its facet. (ii) The centralizer of a maximal Q̆_p-split torus of G is R-smooth. (iii) p does not divide |π_1(G^der)|. (iv) G ⊂ G' = ∏_{i=1}^s Res_{F_i/Q_p} H_i, where each H_i is a reductive F_i-group split over a tamely ramified extension of F_i, and G^der = G'^der. Let ρ'_i : H_i → GL(W_i) be faithful minuscule representations over F_i such that ρ' : G' → ∏_i Res_{F_i/Q_p}GL(W_i) → GL(⊕_i V_i) = GL(V) gives a local Hodge embedding (G',μ') ↪ (GL(V),μ_d). Here V_i is W_i viewed as a Q_p-space and μ' is μ composed with G ⊂ G'. Assume also that ρ := ρ'|_G gives a Hodge embedding (G,μ) ↪ (GL(V),μ_d). Then there is a periodic Z_p-lattice chain L in V and an integral Hodge embedding (𝒢,μ) ↪ (GL(L),μ_d) extending ρ that is very good at all points of M^loc_{𝒢,μ}. Equivalently, set Λ := tot(L) ⊂ V^{⊕r}, with r the number of lattices in a determining segment of L. Then ρ^{⊕r} extends to an integral Hodge embedding (𝒢,μ) ↪ (GL(Λ),μ_{rd}) that is very good at all points of M^loc_{𝒢,μ}.

items.statement: Let V be a K-vector space of dimension 2n with a perfect symmetric K-bilinear form h. items.statement: Case (a) of §6.2.2. Let V ≅ K^{2n} carry a perfect symmetric K-bilinear form h, let G' = GO^+(V,h), and let τ : G' ↪ GL(V) be the natural embedding. Using a Lagrangian basis of (V_0,S), σ_{V_0} is isomorphic to the orthogonal direct sum of s copies of σ_{K^2}, the case V_0 = K^2 with its standard alternating form. items.name: Quaternionic PEL tensor realization
items.statement: Case (b) of §6.2.2. Let D be a quaternion division K-algebra with main involution d ↦ d̄. Let T ≅ D^n be a left D-module with a nondegenerate quaternionic antihermitian form φ : T × T → D, and let G' = GU^+(T,φ), the neutral component of the unitary similitude group. Put ψ(t_1,t_2) = Tr_{D/K}(φ(t_1,t_2)), where Tr_{D/K} is the reduced trace. Then GU(T,φ) = GL_D(T) ∩ GSp(T,ψ), which gives σ : G' ↪ GSp(T,ψ) ↪ GL(T). More generally, let T_0 ≅ D^s be a right D-module with a nondegenerate quaternionic hermitian form S for the main involution. Then W = T_0 ⊗_D T carries the alternating K-form ψ(t_0⊗t, t'_0⊗t') = Tr_{D/K}(S(t'_0,t_0)φ(t,t')). One has GU(T,φ) = GL_{End_D(T_0)}(W) ∩ GSp(W,ψ), which gives σ_{T_0} : G' ↪ GSp(W,ψ) ↪ GL(W). Both σ and σ_{T_0} give local Hodge embeddings for (G,μ). Taking T_0 = D with S(d,d') = d̄d' recovers W = T and σ = σ_D. Since S is standard in a suitable D-basis [Sh73], σ_{T_0} is isomorphic to the orthogonal sum of s copies of σ_D. Let L/K be the unramified quadratic extension, with L ⊂ D. Then D = L ⊕ LΠ with Π^2 = π, D ⊗_K L ≅ M_2(L), and Morita equivalence gives T_L = L^2 ⊗_L V_L with dim_L V_L = 2n. The form φ ⊗ L is determined by a symmetric L-form h_L [RZ96, Prop. A.53], and (G',σ_D) ⊗_K L ≅ (GO^+(V_L,h_L), σ_{L^2}) of case (a).

Case (b): take σ = σ_D : G' → GL(W), W = D ⊗_D T, and let L/K be the unramified quadratic extension, with L ⊂ D. items.statement: §6.3.1. Let D be a central division K-algebra, A = M_m(D) and G = A^* = Res_{K/Q_p}GL_m(D). Let V = D^m, viewed as a Q_p-space, with ρ : G → GL(V) given by left multiplication of A. Let V̄ = D^{opp,m}, with ρ̄ : G → GL(V̄) under which x ∈ A acts by left multiplication by x^{-1}; this is the contragredient. For a local model triple (G,μ,𝒢) put μ' = ρ∘μ and μ̄' = ρ̄∘μ. By [BT84], each x ∈ B(G,Q_p) corresponds to a graded periodic right O_D-lattice chain (L,c) in V. By [BT84, 3.6, Thm], 𝒢 = 𝒢_x is the group scheme of O_D-automorphisms of L, which gives a closed immersion 𝒢 ↪ GL(L). Similarly there is an O_D-lattice chain L̄ in V̄ such that 𝒢 is the stabilizer of L̄ under ρ̄, together with a bijection Λ_i ↦ Λ̄_i between determining segments identifying the stabilizers of Λ_i and Λ̄_i. This gives a closed immersion 𝒢 ↪ GL(L̄).

items.name: Deligne vertex and CM scalar data
items.statement: Let (G_2,X_2) be of abelian type with G_2^ad ≅ Res_{F/Q}H Q-simple, H absolutely simple over the totally real field F. Let I be the set of real places, D = ⊔_{v∈I} D_v the Dynkin diagram, and D_nc, D_c the noncompact and compact parts. S ⊂ D is a set of vertices with (1) S stable under Gal(Q̄/Q) and (2) S ∩ D_nc contained in the underlined vertices of [De79, 1.3.9]. In §7.2.3 it is chosen as follows: S maximal if (G_2^ad,X_2^ad) is neither of type A nor of type D^H; S = {ϖ_{v,1}, ϖ_{v,n} : v ∈ I} for type A_n (then K_S is a CM extension of F for n ≥ 2); S = {ϖ_{v,1} : v ∈ I} for type D^H_n (then K_S = F). W is a Q-representation of G^sc with W_C ≅ ⊕_{s∈S} W(s)^n. K_S is the product of totally real or CM fields with Hom(K_S,C) = S, acting on W. The largest quotient of G^sc through which G^sc → GL(W) factors is Res_{F/Q}H^♯. K is a CM extension of F disjoint from K_S in which every prime of F above p splits. T is a set of embeddings K → C as in [KP18, Lemma 4.6.22].

items.name: Correct topology for the divided-power logarithm tail
items.statement: Correction to the proof of [KP18, Lem. 3.1.17], pointed out by M. Hoff. Let A be complete local and p-torsion free with 𝔐_A^N ⊂ pA. Then Ŵ(A)[1/p] is not complete for the topology τ of KP18. It is complete and separated for the p-adic topology (neighbourhoods p^nŴ(A)), because Ŵ(𝔐_A) is closed in W(𝔐_A) and p-adically complete and separated [Zi01, Prop. 2.3, 2.4]. For x ∈ Ŵ(𝔐_A)[1/p], p^{-m}φ^m(x) → 0 in this topology: reduce to x ∈ Ŵ(p𝔐_A) using [Zi01, Lem. 2.2], then for p > 2 use Zink's logarithmic coordinates, in which p^{-m}φ^m is the shift [z_i] ↦ [z_{m+i}] ([Zi02, (49), p.35]). This completes the proof.

items.name: Multiplier exact sequences for a Hodge-type group
items.statement: Let (G, X) be of Hodge type with G^ad simple, G^c the subgroup generated by G^der and the largest compact subtorus Z_{G,0} of Z_G, and Z^c_G the subgroup generated by Z_{G^der} and Z_{G,0}. Then 1 → G^c → G → G_m → 1 and 1 → Z^c_G → Z_G → G_m → 1 are exact, the maps to G_m being the symplectic multiplier of some (equivalently any) Hodge embedding.
