items.name: Shimura datum of Hodge type
items.statement: A Shimura datum (G,X) (Deligne) is of Hodge type if there is an embedding of Shimura data (G,X) ↪ (GSp_{2g}, S^±) into the Shimura datum of a symplectic similitude group.
items.note: Only the global definition. B's M01 is the local version. Needed for the abelian-type definition and for §7. Planned: ShimuraData D4 plans the definitions of Hodge-type and abelian-type Shimura data.

items.name: Shimura datum of abelian type
items.statement: A Shimura datum (G,X) is of abelian type if there are a Shimura datum (G_1,X_1) of Hodge type and a central isogeny G_1^der → G^der that induces an isomorphism (G_1^ad, X_1^ad) ≅ (G^ad, X^ad).
items.note: The main theorem (Theorem 1.1.1 = Theorem 7.2.21) is stated for this class. It is defined only in the introduction. B's M02 is the local analogue (Def. 3.1.3). Planned: ShimuraData D4 plans the definitions of Hodge-type and abelian-type Shimura data.

items.name: Stabilizer and parahoric level subgroups at p
items.statement: Fix p > 2 and a prime v of E above p, and set E = E_v. Let 𝒢 be a Bruhat–Tits stabilizer group scheme over Z_p with generic fibre G = G_{Q_p}, and 𝒢° its neutral component (the parahoric). Put K_p = 𝒢(Z_p) (stabilizer level) and K_p° = 𝒢°(Z_p) (parahoric level). For sufficiently small compact open K^p ⊂ G(A_f^p) put K° = K^p K_p° and K = K^p K_p, giving Sh_{K°}(G,X) and Sh_K(G,X) over E.
items.note: The level structure in Theorem 1.1.1. Footnote 1 (p. 2): some results extend to quasi-parahoric K_p [DvHKZ]. Missing: routed to route 8.

items.name: Classical tamely ramified group and splitting data (H_0, K̃, e, π̃)
items.statement: A reductive G over K is classical if G^ad has no exceptional factors (by convention triality forms are also excluded). Let H_0 be the Chevalley (split) form of G over Z_p. G is tamely ramified if there is a finite tame Galois extension K̃/K of ramification degree e, Γ = Gal(K̃/K), with G ⊗_K K̃ ≅ H_0 ⊗_{Z_p} K̃. Enlarging K̃ by an unramified extension, one may assume K̃ contains a uniformizer π̃ with π̃^e ∈ K^un, where K^un is the maximal unramified extension of K in K̃.
items.note: These are the standing hypotheses of Prop. 2.2.2, §2.4.4 and §3.3.1. The π̃ normalization is used in §2.3.6. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Point generic in its facet
items.statement: A point x ∈ B(G,K) is generic in its facet if 𝒢_x = 𝒢_{x'} for all x' in some open neighbourhood of x in that facet.
items.note: Used in Prop. 2.2.2, §2.4.4 and throughout §3 and §6 ('x generic in its facet'). Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Connected stabilizers are generic-point stabilizers
items.statement: If x ∈ B(G,K) and 𝒢_x is connected, and y ∈ B(G,K) is generic in the smallest facet containing x, then 𝒢_y = 𝒢_x. Hence Proposition 2.2.2 applies to every stabilizer group scheme that is parahoric (connected).
items.note: The paper gives no proof. It follows because stabilizers are locally constant near y, so Stab(y) fixes the facet pointwise and hence fixes x, while 𝒢_y ⊇ 𝒢_y° = 𝒢_x° = 𝒢_x. This is what lets the parahoric case of Theorem 1.1.1 use Prop. 2.2.2. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Building of GL(V) via graded periodic lattice chains; parahoric GL(ℒ)
items.statement: Fix a volume form ∧^{dim V}V ≅ K. Then B(GL(V),K) is identified with pairs (ℒ,c), where ℒ = {Λ_•} is a periodic O-lattice chain in V and c: ℒ → ℝ is a grading ([BT84], [KaP23, Cor. 5.1.28]). For x = (ℒ,c), the parahoric subgroup is the common stabilizer of the lattices in ℒ, equivalently of a determining segment Λ_s = πΛ_0 ⊂ Λ_{s−1} ⊂ ⋯ ⊂ Λ_0. The parahoric group scheme GL(ℒ) is the smooth affine model determined ([BTII, Prop. 1.7.6]) by GL(ℒ)(Ŏ) = ∩_i GL(Λ_i ⊗_O Ŏ) = ∩_{i=0}^{s−1} GL(Λ_i ⊗_O Ŏ).
items.note: D03 defines the chain, but no item defines the group scheme GL(ℒ), which is the source of Lemma 2.3.1 (T08) and the target of Lemma 2.3.3 (T09). Planned: ReductiveGroupsPartII RG2.2 plans the GL_n building as norms and lattice chains; ReductiveGroupsPartII RG2.3 plans the stabilizer and parahoric group schemes of facets.

items.name: Γ-fixed building point of a Γ-stable lattice
items.statement: Let K̃/K be finite tame Galois with group Γ, inertia I and e = |I|, and let Λ̃ ⊂ V ⊗_K K̃ be a Γ-stable Õ-lattice. The chain ℒ̃ = {π̃^iΛ̃} with grading c̃(π̃^iΛ̃) = i is a periodic graded Õ-lattice chain. It gives a Γ-fixed point x̃ ∈ B(GL(V),K̃), whose parahoric is GL(Λ̃). By (2.1.3), x̃ corresponds to x ∈ B(GL(V),K) with graded chain (ℒ,c), and GL(ℒ) = (Res_{Õ/O}GL(Λ̃))^Γ.
items.note: This sets up Lemma 2.3.3 (T09), which then identifies ℒ explicitly as {(π̃^iΛ̃)^Γ}. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Closed immersion of the stabilizer into GL(Λ̃) (2.4.5)
items.statement: Let G and K̃/K be as in §2.2 (with the hypotheses of Prop. 2.2.2), and ρ: G → GL(V) a faithful representation over K. Let x ∈ B(G,K) be generic in its facet, replaced by a nearby point with the same stabilizer so that x is hyperspecial in B(G,K̃) and 𝒢̃_x is reductive (Prop. 2.2.2). By Prop. 2.4.2 there is a Γ-stable Õ-lattice Λ̃ ⊂ V ⊗_K K̃ such that ρ extends to a closed immersion 𝒢̃_x ↪ GL(Λ̃). Applying Res_{Õ/O} and Γ-fixed points gives the closed immersion ρ: 𝒢_x = (Res_{Õ/O}𝒢̃_x)^Γ ↪ (Res_{Õ/O}GL(Λ̃))^Γ ↪ GL(Λ̃), with Λ̃ viewed as an O-module.
items.note: T12 covers Remark 2.4.3 but not this construction of the embedding of 𝒢_x, which feeds §3.3 and §6. On generic fibres the composite is ρ ⊗_K K̃ viewed over K, which is ≅ ρ^{⊕[K̃:K]}; the paper still calls it ρ. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Edixhoven's lemma (cited)
items.statement: [Ed92, 3.4 Prop.] Let K̃/K be a finite tamely ramified Galois extension with group Γ, and X a smooth (quasi-projective, here affine) Õ-scheme with an Õ-semilinear Γ-action. Then the fixed-point scheme (Res_{Õ/O}X)^Γ is smooth over O.
items.locator: Proof of Proposition 2.2.2, p. 11; Remark 2.4.3(b), p. 15; §1.2.3, p. 6
items.note: Black box. Tameness is used exactly here. It gives smoothness of (Res 𝒢̃_{x'})^Γ and (Res GL(Λ̃))^Γ, and so the identification with 𝒢_x via [BTII, 1.7.6]. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Smooth models are determined by Ŏ-points (cited)
items.statement: [BTII, Prop. 1.7.6] Over a henselian DVR O with strict henselization Ŏ, a smooth affine O-group scheme with given generic fibre G is determined up to unique isomorphism by its group of Ŏ-points in G(K̆). A homomorphism of generic fibres extends to a homomorphism of such smooth models if and only if it maps Ŏ-points into Ŏ-points.
items.locator: §2.3, p. 12; proof of Lemma 2.3.3, p. 13; proof of Proposition 2.4.2, p. 14
items.note: Black box, also used implicitly in the proof of Prop. 2.2.2. In Prop. 2.4.2 it is applied over O_M, which is strictly henselian but not complete. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Homomorphisms from reductive group schemes are closed immersions for p odd (cited)
items.statement: [PrY06, (Cor.) 1.3] Let 𝒢 be a reductive group scheme over a DVR whose residue characteristic is p > 2, and f: 𝒢 → GL(Λ) a homomorphism whose generic fibre is a closed immersion. Then f is a closed immersion.
items.locator: Proof of Proposition 2.4.2, p. 14 (also used in §3.3); also §3.3.9 (p. 22), §3.3.11 (p. 23), proof of Theorem 3.3.25 (p. 26)
items.note: This is the only place p > 2 enters Prop. 2.4.2. (In [PrY06] the exceptions in residue characteristic 2 involve SO_{2n+1} factors.) Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Tame subdivision: nearby points hyperspecial over a tame extension (cited)
items.statement: [PR24b, Prop. 2.7, Prop. 2.8, Rem. 2.9] Let G be absolutely simple and simply connected, split over a tame extension, with p odd, and, in type A, the division-algebra index prime to p. For x ∈ B(G,K), a 'tame subdivision' of the apartment gives points x' in the facet of x, as close to x as desired, that are hyperspecial in B(G,L̃) for a finite tame extension L̃/K. Hence statement (*) of the proof of Prop. 2.2.2 holds for such G.
items.note: Black box. The type-A index hypothesis of Prop. 2.2.2 enters only here. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Extended-building stabilizers via the Kottwitz homomorphism (cited)
items.statement: [HR08, Rem. 11], [BTII, 4.2.16]: G(K̆)_x = G(K̆)_x̄ ∩ G(K̆)^1. Here G(K̆)_x̄ is the stabilizer of the image x̄ ∈ B̄(G,K̆), and G(K̆)^1 is the kernel of G(K̆) →κ_G π_1(G)_I → π_1(G)_I/torsion, with κ_G the Kottwitz homomorphism and π_1(G) Borovoi's fundamental group (cocharacters modulo coroots, §1.5). Moreover 𝒢_x(Ŏ)/𝒢_x°(Ŏ) is finite abelian [HR08].
items.locator: §2.1.1, p. 9; proof of Proposition 2.2.2, p. 12; §1.5, p. 9
items.note: Black box used in the reductive case of Prop. 2.2.2. Could instead be merged into P02 (see the fix there). Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: lft Néron models of tori and Weil restriction (cited)
items.statement: [BLR90, §10] A torus T over K has an lft Néron model 𝒯. For a finite extension K̃/K, with 𝒯̃ the lft Néron model of T_{K̃}, the Weil restriction Res_{Õ/O}𝒯̃ is the lft Néron model of Res_{K̃/K}T_{K̃}.
items.note: Needed to make sense of the R-smoothness definition (D02). Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Closed immersion of finite-type Néron models of centralizers (cited)
items.statement: [KZ25, Lem. 2.4.4], as used in the proof of Prop. 2.1.5(3). Let T be the centralizer of a maximal K̆-split torus S of the R-smooth group G whose apartment contains x, and T' the centralizer of a maximal K̆-split torus of G' containing the image of S. Then T → T' extends to a closed immersion of finite-type Néron models. Combined with the argument of [KZ25, Prop. 2.4.10], this gives Prop. 2.1.5(3).
items.note: Black box. I could not check the exact hypotheses of [KZ25, Lem. 2.4.4]. The statement records what the proof uses. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Invariant lattice for a bounded group with compact Galois action (cited argument)
items.statement: [Ki10, Lem. 2.3.1] (the argument). Let M be the maximal unramified extension of K̃. There is a Gal(M/K)-stable O_M-lattice Λ_M ⊂ V ⊗_K M that is also stable under ρ(𝒢̃(O_M)). One takes the O_M-span of the orbit of a lattice under the semidirect product 𝒢̃(O_M) ⋊ Gal(M/K), which is bounded, so the span is a lattice over the DVR O_M.
items.note: Black box ('apply the same argument as in [Ki10, Lem. 2.3.1]'). It is elementary, and I checked that it works here. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Hyperspecial points under field extension and passage to the derived group
items.statement: (i) A point that is hyperspecial in B(G,K̃) stays hyperspecial in B(G,K̃') for every finite extension K̃'/K̃. (ii) For a split group H, a point x ∈ B(H,K) is hyperspecial if and only if its image x̄ ∈ B̄(H,K) = B(H^der,K) is hyperspecial.
items.note: The proof asserts both without proof or citation. Both are standard. (ii) is misprinted as B(H^der, K̃); see sourceIssues. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Local model triple, morphisms, reflex field
items.statement: Let F/Q_p be finite. A local model triple (G,{μ},G) over F consists of a connected reductive group G over F, the G(F̄)-conjugacy class {μ} of a minuscule cocharacter μ: G_{m,F̄} → G_F̄, and a quasi-parahoric stabilizer group scheme G over O_F for G. A morphism (G,{μ},G) → (G′,{μ′},G′) is a group scheme homomorphism G → G′ taking {μ} to {μ′}. E denotes the reflex field of (G,{μ}), a subfield of F̄ containing F. Notation: (G,μ) for (G,{μ}) and (G,μ) for (G,{μ},G).
items.note: Basic object of §3–§7; no existing item. Missing: routed to route 4.

items.name: Integral Hodge embedding
items.statement: An integral Hodge embedding for (G,μ) is a closed immersion of group schemes G ↪ GL(Λ) over O_F, with Λ an O_F-lattice in V, whose generic fibre G ↪ GL(V) is a Hodge embedding in the sense of Definition 3.1.2.
items.note: Used in §3.1.9, Lemma 3.4.1, Definition 3.4.4; M01 covers only Hodge type. Missing: routed to route 4.

items.name: Essentially tame reductive group
items.statement: A reductive group G over F is essentially tame if G^ad is quasi-tame (Definition 3.1.4(1)), cf. [PR24, App.].
items.note: Used in standard assumptions 3.1.5; D04 covers only (1). Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Nontrivial adjoint factors of abelian-type pairs are classical and tame (cited)
items.statement: Suppose p > 2 and (G,μ) is of abelian type, and write (G^ad, μ^ad) ≃ (∏_{i=1}^s Res_{K_i/F}H_i, {μ_i}) with H_i absolutely simple over K_i. If μ_i ≠ 1, then H_i is of classical type (A, B, C or D; triality forms of D_4 excluded) and splits over a tamely ramified extension of K_i. If p > 3, every reductive group over F is essentially tame; if p = 3, the groups that are not essentially tame are triality forms. (Cited: [PR26, Prop. 7.2.1 and its proof], cf. [De79, §2.3.8].)
items.note: Black box. Needed in §3.4.2 to apply Theorem 3.3.25 (classical H′_i) to the group G′ of Prop. 3.2.11, and it explains why the standard assumptions matter only on μ-trivial factors. Missing: routed to route 4.

items.name: Scholze–Weinstein conjecture for GL (cited)
items.statement: For an O_F-lattice Λ and the standard minuscule μ_d, Gr(d,Λ)^◇ = M^v_{GL(Λ),μ_d} ([SW20, Cor. 21.6.10 and its proof]); hence 𝕄^loc_{GL(Λ),μ_d} = Gr(d,Λ), the smooth Grassmannian of d-dimensional subspaces of Λ.
items.locator: §3.1.9, p. 17; reused in the proof of Lemma 3.4.1, p. 28
items.note: Black box from SW20. Missing: routed to route 4.

items.name: Weil restriction of Bruhat–Tits stabilizers (cited)
items.statement: If G ≅ Res_{K/F}H and G is the stabilizer of x ∈ B(G,F) = B(H,K), then G ≅ Res_{O_K/O_F}ℋ with ℋ the stabilizer of x for H ([HR20, Prop. 4.7]).
items.note: Black box. Missing: routed to route 4.

items.name: Generic fibre of the Beilinson–Drinfeld Grassmannian
items.statement: For a K_0-algebra R, the completion of R[u] along (E(u)) contains the completion of K_0[u] along (E(u)), which is identified with K[[t]] by a map sending t to E(u) and inducing the identity on residue fields; hence the completion of R[u] is identified with (K ⊗_{K_0} R)[[t]] (t ↦ E(u)). This gives an isomorphism of the generic fibre of Fl^{E(u)}_{H̲°,0} with Gr_{Res_{K/K_0}H} (cf. [HR20, Cor. 3.5]), and of the generic fibre of Fl^{E(u)}_{H̲°} with Gr_{Res_{K/F}H} ≅ Gr_G.
items.note: Needed to make sense of S_μ inside the generic fibre in Definition 3.2.6. Partly cited. Missing: routed to route 4.

items.name: Construction of M^loc_{G,μ} via an auxiliary Hodge-type group
items.statement: Assume (G,{μ},G) satisfies the standard assumptions 3.1.5. Write G^ad = G^ad_1 × G^ad_2, where G^ad_1 (resp. G^ad_2) is the product of the F-simple factors on which μ^ad is nontrivial (resp. trivial). Let G_1 = ker(G → G^ad_2); {μ} factors through G_1, giving {μ_1}. Then G_1 → G^ad_1 is a central extension and (G_1,μ_1) is of abelian type and satisfies the hypotheses of Prop. 3.2.11. Let (G′,μ′) be as in its conclusion and define M^loc_{G,μ} := M_{G′,μ′} ⊗_{O_{E′}} O_E (3.2.13). This is a flat projective O_E-scheme with reduced special fibre (Theorem 3.2.9). (G′ is the stabilizer group scheme of G′ corresponding to G; this is left implicit here and made explicit only in §4.4, p. 46.)
items.note: Central construction of §3; not an existing item (M20 cites it only indirectly). Remark 3.2.14: when p divides |π₁(G^der)|, M^loc and M_{G,μ} need not be isomorphic ([HLR24]). Missing: routed to route 4.

items.name: Embedding into the Weil restriction of the split form
items.statement: In the setting of §3.3.1 (G = Res_{K/F}H, H tame, x generic satisfying Prop. 2.2.2, ℋ = ℋ_x, G = 𝒢_x ≅ Res_{O_K/O_F}ℋ, K̃/K, Γ, x′ as in Prop. 2.2.2, H⊗_K K̃ ≃ H_0 ⊗_{Z_p} K̃ with H_0 the Chevalley form, ℋ̃ = ℋ̃_{x′} ≃ H_0 ⊗ O_K̃ hyperspecial, ℋ ≃ (Res_{O_K̃/O_K}ℋ̃)^Γ): the map (3.3.2) G = Res_{K/F}H → Res_{K̃/F}(H_0⊗K̃) extends to a closed immersion (3.3.3) G = Res_{O_K/O_F}ℋ → Res_{O_K̃/O_F}(H_0⊗O_K̃) (Prop. 2.1.5). With μ̃ = μ composed with (3.3.2) and Ẽ its reflex field, (Res_{K̃/F}(H_0⊗K̃), {μ̃}, Res_{O_K̃/O_F}(H_0⊗O_K̃)) is a local model triple and (3.3.4) is a morphism of local model triples.
items.note: Set-up used by Prop. 3.3.7, Theorem 3.3.25 and §3.4.5. Missing: routed to route 4.

items.name: Γ-fixed-point group scheme over O_0[u] and the map (3.3.6)
items.statement: After possibly enlarging K̃ (e = ramification index of K̃/K), choose uniformizers π of K and π̃ of K̃ with π̃^e = π, and identify Γ with the Galois group of O_{K̃_0}[ũ^±]/O_{K_0}[u^±], u ↦ ũ^e (compatible with u ↦ π, ũ ↦ π̃). Write O_0 = O_{K_0}, Õ_0 = O_{K̃_0}. Then H̲ := (Res_{Õ_0[ũ]/O_0[u]}(H_0 ⊗ Õ_0[ũ]))^Γ is a smooth affine O_0[u]-group scheme (Edixhoven's lemma); the group H̲° of [Le16, Thm. 3.3] is its neutral component (cf. [PZ13, §4.2.1]); H̲ → Res_{Õ_0[ũ]/O_0[u]}(H_0⊗Õ_0[ũ]) is a closed immersion lifting (3.3.3), and H̲° → Res(…) is a locally closed immersion. This gives the morphism (3.3.6) Fl^{E(u)}_{H̲°} → Fl^{E(u)}_{Res_{Õ_0[ũ]/O_0[u]}(H_0⊗Õ_0[ũ])} of Beilinson–Drinfeld Grassmannians over O_F.
items.note: Input to Prop. 3.3.7. Missing: routed to route 4.

items.name: Weyl-module Z_p-form of a representation
items.statement: Let H_0 be split reductive over Z_p, L/Q_p a field, ρ: H_0⊗L → GL(V), T_0 ≃ G_m^r ⊂ B_0 ⊂ H_0, {λ_1,…,λ_n} the distinct highest weights of V, V_{Z_p}(λ_i) the Weyl modules. Then V ≃ ⊕_i V_{Z_p}(λ_i)^{⊕m_i} ⊗ L (m_i ≥ 1) equivariantly. Λ_0 := ⊕_i V_{Z_p}(λ_i)^{⊕m_i} carries ρ_0: H_0 → GL(Λ_0); if ρ_0⊗L ≃ ρ is faithful, ρ_0 is a closed immersion ([PrY06, Cor. 1.3]).
items.note: Used in §3.3.11, Theorem 3.3.25 and Prop. 3.4.6. Missing: routed to route 3.

items.name: Closed immersion of Weil-restricted BD Grassmannians
items.statement: The homomorphism ρ̲_0 = ρ_0 ⊗ Õ_0[ũ]: H_0⊗Õ_0[ũ] → GL(Λ_0⊗Õ_0[ũ]) and its restriction of scalars (3.3.12) Res_{Õ_0[ũ]/O_0[u]}(H_0⊗Õ_0[ũ]) → Res_{Õ_0[ũ]/O_0[u]}GL(Λ_0⊗Õ_0[ũ]) are closed immersions; (3.3.12) specializes under u ↦ π to Res_{O_K̃/O_K}(ρ_0⊗O_K̃). The induced morphism (3.3.13) of affine Grassmannians Fl^{E(u)}_{Res(H_0⊗Õ_0[ũ])} → Fl^{E(u)}_{Res(GL(Λ_0⊗Õ_0[ũ]))} is a monomorphism, hence a closed immersion of ind-projective ind-schemes over O_F.
items.note: Step behind Prop. 3.3.14. Missing: routed to route 4.

items.name: Weil restriction of torsors identifies BD Grassmannians (cited)
items.statement: [HR20, Cor. 3.6] (as used): for a finite flat Spec(B) → Spec(A) of polynomial rings as in the text, Weil restriction of torsors gives isomorphisms of Beilinson–Drinfeld Grassmannians. Examples: (3.3.17) Fl^{E(u)}_{Res_{Õ_0[ũ]/O_0[u]}GL(Λ_0⊗Õ_0[ũ])} ≅ Fl^{Ẽ(ũ)}_{GL(Λ_0⊗Õ_0[ũ])} for u ↦ ũ^e, with Ẽ(ũ) = E(ũ^e) the Eisenstein polynomial of π̃; and Fl^{E(u)}_{GL̲,0} ≅ Fl^{v−π_F}_{GL̲_{K/K_0},0} for r: O_0[v] → O_0[u], v ↦ E(u)+π_F. These identify the two a priori different constructions of M_{Res_{O_K̃/O_F}GL(Λ_0⊗O_K̃),μ̃′} and M_{Res_{O_K̃/O_F}(H_0⊗O_K̃),μ̃}.
items.note: Black box; needed to compare the targets in Props. 3.3.7 and 3.3.14. Missing: routed to route 4.

items.name: Weil restriction of GL into GL of the restricted lattice
items.statement: For K/F finite and an O_K-lattice Λ, the natural homomorphism Res_{O_K/O_F}GL(Λ) → GL(Λ^{(O_F)}) (3.3.19) is a closed immersion (Λ^{(O_F)} is Λ with its O_F-module structure by restriction).
items.note: Stated with 'easily see … by writing down the equations'. Missing: routed to route 4.

items.name: Locally closed immersion of affine flag varieties (cited)
items.statement: [PR08, Thm. 1.4] (as used): a closed immersion of (parahoric) group schemes over k[[v]] of the type in the proof of Prop. 3.3.20 induces a locally closed immersion of affine flag varieties; hence ι ⊗_{O_F} k is a locally closed immersion, and a closed immersion because its source is ind-projective.
items.note: Black box. Missing: routed to route 4.

items.name: Closed-immersion argument of [PZ13, Prop. 8.1] (cited method)
items.statement: (As used) If a morphism between the flat projective local models (closures of generic fibres in BD Grassmannians over O_E) is a closed immersion on special fibres, then it is a closed immersion (Nakayama). The special-fibre closed immersion comes from the map of affine flag varieties restricted to the local model.
items.locator: Proof of Prop. 3.3.7 (p. 21), Prop. 3.3.20 (p. 25), ι′ in the proof of Prop. 3.3.20; cf. §6
items.note: Black box method invoked three times without restatement. Missing: routed to route 4.

items.name: Hodge embeddings of product form (3.3.24) and their direct sums
items.statement: For (G,{μ},G) with G quasi-tame, G ≃ ∏_{i=1}^r Res_{K_i/F}H_i (H_i tame), so that (G,{μ}) is a product of local Shimura pairs (Res_{K_i/F}H_i,{μ_i}), and faithful minuscule ρ_i: H_i → GL(V_i) over K_i with Res_{K_i/F}H_i → Res_{K_i/F}GL(V_i) ↪ GL(V_i^{(F)}) Hodge embeddings: ρ: G ≃ ∏ Res_{K_i/F}H_i → ∏ Res_{K_i/F}GL(V_i) ↪ GL(V), V = ⊕_i V_i^{(F)}, is a Hodge embedding (3.3.24), so (G,{μ}) is of Hodge type; for every m ≥ 1, ρ^{⊕m}: G → GL(V^{⊕m}) is again a Hodge embedding of the same form.
items.note: Hypothesis format of Theorem 3.3.25. Missing: routed to route 4.

items.name: Diamond of a Zariski closure is the v-sheaf closure (implicit input)
items.statement: (As used) For the flat projective O_E-scheme X̄_μ given as the Zariski closure of X_μ in Gr(d,Λ)_{O_E}, the v-sheaf (X̄_μ)^◇ over Spd(O_E) equals the v-sheaf closure (X_μ^◇)^− of X_μ^◇ in (Gr(d,Λ)_{O_E})^◇.
items.note: Stated without reference; standard for flat proper schemes. Missing: routed to route 6.

items.name: M^v_{G,μ} is closed in the GL(Λ) BD Grassmannian (implicit input)
items.statement: (Needed) For an integral Hodge embedding G ↪ GL(Λ), the functorial map M^v_{G,μ} → Gr_{GL(Λ),Spd(O_E)} is a closed immersion, so M^v_{G,μ} is the v-sheaf closure of X_μ^◇ in Gr_{GL(Λ),Spd(O_E)}.
items.locator: Proof of Lemma 3.4.1, p. 28 ('By definition, this last closure is M^v_{G,μ}')
items.note: The paper asserts this 'by definition' (see source issue). Standard ingredients: Gr_G → Gr_{GL} is a monomorphism, M^v_{G,μ} is proper, and a proper monomorphism is a closed immersion. Compare FOUND.json I10 (DvHKZ Lemma A.3.5). Missing: routed to route 4.

items.name: Good Hodge embeddings through the Weyl-module lattice
items.statement: §3.4.5: Let G ≅ Res_{K/F}H with H split over a tame extension of K, p ∤ |π₁(G^der)|, G = 𝒢_x with x generic in its facet, H^ad without factors involving division algebras of index divisible by p (and H classical, implicitly). If there is a faithful minuscule ρ_1: H → GL(V) over K with Res_{K/F}H → Res_{K/F}GL(V) ↪ GL(V) a Hodge embedding, then (G,{μ},G) admits good integral Hodge embeddings, namely G ↪ Res_{O_K̃/O_F}(H_0⊗O_K̃) ↪ Res_{O_K̃/O_F}GL(Λ_0⊗O_K̃) ↪ GL(Λ_0⊗O_K̃), where K̃/K is tame with x hyperspecial over K̃ and Λ_0⊗O_K̃ ⊂ V⊗_K K̃ is viewed as an O_F-lattice.
items.note: Justified by 'the proof of Theorem 3.2.15' (Theorem 3.3.25 first case + Theorem 3.2.9 + Lemma 3.4.1); used in the proof of Prop. 3.4.6. Missing: routed to route 4.

items.name: Points t^μ and the affine Schubert variety S_μ
items.statement: For μ ∈ X_*(T), t^μ ∈ LG(k) is the k((t))-point of G induced by μ; its image in Gr_G = LG/L^+G is also written t^μ. For μ ∈ X_*(T)^+, the affine Schubert variety S_μ = S_μ^G ⊂ Gr_G is the reduced closure of the G(k[[t]])-orbit of t^μ.
items.note: Used in every statement of §4. Gr_G itself is from §3.2.1 (outside this range). Missing: routed to route 4.

items.name: Closure relations and orbit stratification of affine Schubert varieties
items.statement: For λ, μ ∈ X_*(T)^+: S_λ ⊂ S_μ if and only if λ ≼ μ. Moreover S_μ(k) is the union of the G(k[[t]])-orbits of t^λ for λ ∈ X_*(T)^+ with λ ≼ μ.
items.locator: §4.1.1, p.31 (first part, stated without reference); used for t^λ ∈ S_μ in §4.1.7 and in the proof of Theorem 4.1.6 (§4.3.15, p.45)
items.note: Standard black box; the paper gives no citation. Missing: routed to route 4.

items.name: Open chart of Gr_G at t^λ (cited)
items.statement: Let L^−G(R) = G(R[t^{−1}]) and L^{−−}G = ker(L^−G → G, t^{−1} ↦ 0). For λ ∈ X_*(T)^+, the map t^λL^{−−}Gt^{−λ} → Gr_G, g ↦ gt^λ, is representable by an open immersion sending 1 to t^λ. Hence T_{t^λ}Gr_G ≅ t^λ Lie(L^{−−}G) t^{−λ} ≅ ⊕_{α∈R} t^{⟨λ,α⟩−1}k[t^{−1}]X_α ⊕ t^{−1}k[t^{−1}]𝔱.
items.note: R06 records the decomposition but not the cited open-immersion input. The paper prints 't ↦ 0' for the evaluation t^{−1} ↦ 0. Missing: routed to route 4.

items.name: Φ^tan_{λ,μ}, 𝔗^tan_{λ,μ} and the decomposition of T_{t^λ}S_μ
items.statement: Let λ, μ ∈ X_*(T)^+ with λ ≼ μ. The torus T̃ = 𝔾_m × T acts on Gr_G, with 𝔾_m by rotation t ↦ at and T by left multiplication. It fixes t^λ ∈ S_μ, so T_{t^λ}S_μ is T̃-stable, and T̃ acts on t^rX_α with weight (r,α) and on t^r𝔱 with weight (r,0). Put Φ^tan_{λ,μ} = {(α,r) ∈ R × ℤ : t^rX_α ∈ T_{t^λ}S_μ} and 𝔗^tan_{λ,μ} = T_{t^λ}S_μ ∩ t^{−1}k[t^{−1}]𝔱. Then T_{t^λ}S_μ = ⊕_{(α,k)∈Φ^tan} k·t^kX_α ⊕ 𝔗^tan_{λ,μ}, and 𝔗^tan = ⊕_{l≥1}(𝔗^tan ∩ t^{−l}𝔱).
items.note: Theorems 4.2.3 and 4.3.2 are equalities for these two pieces. Missing: routed to route 4.

items.name: Root-curve set Φ^cur_{λ,μ}
items.statement: Φ^cur_{λ,μ} = {(α,k) : α ∈ R, ⟨λ,α⟩ − k_α ≤ k ≤ ⟨λ,α⟩ − 1} ⊂ R × ℤ. By Proposition 4.2.2(2), Φ^cur_{λ,μ} ⊂ Φ^tan_{λ,μ}, and each t^kX_α with (α,k) ∈ Φ^cur is the tangent vector at 0 of a curve 𝔸^1 → S_μ through t^λ.
items.note: R19 (Theorem 4.2.3) is the equality Φ^cur = Φ^tan, which no existing item defines. Missing: routed to route 4.

items.name: Reduction of Theorems 4.2.3 and 4.3.2 to G^ad simple and G^der = G^sc (cited inputs)
items.statement: Write G^ad ≅ ∏_{i=1}^r H_i with each H_i simple, and let μ_i, λ_i be the components of μ^ad, λ^ad. There are z-extensions 1 → Z → H̃_i → H_i → 1 with H̃_i^der = H̃_i^sc such that μ_i, λ_i lift to μ̃_i, λ̃_i ∈ X_*(T_i)^+ [MS82, Prop. 3.1]. If p ∤ |π_1(G^der)|, there is an isomorphism ∏_i S_{μ̃_i} ≅ S_μ as in [KP18, Prop. 2.2.7]. It is compatible with the points t^λ, the root curves and the torus actions, so Φ^cur_{λ,μ} = ⊔_i Φ^{H̃_i,cur}_{λ̃_i,μ̃_i} and Φ^tan_{λ,μ} = ⊔_i Φ^{H̃_i,tan}_{λ̃_i,μ̃_i}, and similarly for the Cartan spaces.
items.locator: §4.2.4, p.33; reused for Theorem 4.3.2 on p.40
items.note: Two external black boxes. This is where p ∤ |π_1(G^der)| is used. The paper prints the decompositions as products ∏ (see the new source issue). Missing: routed to route 4.

items.name: Φ^FM_{λ,μ}, 𝔗^FM_{λ,μ} and the chains of inclusions
items.statement: Since S_μ ⊂ S^FM_μ, T_{t^λ}S_μ ⊂ T_{t^λ}S^FM_μ ⊂ T_{t^λ}Gr_G, and T_{t^λ}S^FM_μ is T̃-stable. Put Φ^FM_{λ,μ} = {(α,r) ∈ R × ℤ : t^rX_α ∈ T_{t^λ}S^FM_μ} and 𝔗^FM_{λ,μ} = T_{t^λ}S^FM_μ ∩ t^{−1}k[t^{−1}]𝔱. Then Φ^cur ⊂ Φ^tan ⊂ Φ^FM (§4.2.11) and 𝔗^cur ⊂ 𝔗^tan ⊂ 𝔗^FM (§4.3.3).
items.locator: pp.34–35 (after Remark 4.2.8, before §4.2.9); inclusions in §4.2.11 (p.35) and §4.3.3 (p.40)
items.note: Needed to state Proposition 4.2.10, Proposition 4.3.4 and Remark 4.3.14. Missing: routed to route 4.

items.name: Proposition 4.2.10(1)
items.statement: For λ, μ ∈ X_*(T)^+ with λ ≼ μ and α ∈ R: l_α = l_{−α} + ⟨λ,α⟩.
items.note: The proof uses (ϖ,ϖ′) ∈ 𝒲(α) ⇔ (ϖ,ϖ′+α) ∈ 𝒲(−α). This is valid when 𝒲(α) is read as 'ϖ′ and ϖ′+α are weights', but fails in characteristic p for the literal X_αv ≠ 0 definition (E9, revised). For minuscule ϖ both readings agree, which is all Proposition 4.2.13 uses. Missing: routed to route 2.

items.name: Inequality (4.2.12): k_α ≤ l_α
items.statement: For λ, μ ∈ X_*(T)^+ with λ ≼ μ, k_α ≤ l_α for all α ∈ R. If equality holds for every α, then Φ^cur_{λ,μ} = Φ^tan_{λ,μ} = Φ^FM_{λ,μ}.
items.note: Printed as 'with equality if and only if'; only the 'if' direction is proved or used (new source issue). The inequality rests on Proposition 4.2.10(2) (E9). Missing: routed to route 2.

items.name: Lattices P, P^∨ and lifted fundamental weights Ω, Ω^min
items.statement: P (resp. P^∨) is the weight (resp. coweight) lattice, the ℤ-dual of the coroot (resp. root) lattice. There are natural maps X^*(T) → P and X_*(T) → P^∨, and P^+, P^{∨,+} denote the dominant elements. If G^der = G^sc, the map X^*(T) → P is surjective. Ω = {ϖ_1,…,ϖ_n} ⊂ P^+ are the fundamental weights for Δ = {α_1,…,α_n}, each lifted to X^*(T)^+ (still written ϖ_i). Ω^min ⊂ Ω is the subset of minuscule fundamental weights.
items.note: Complements R31 (the minuscule predicate). Missing: routed to route 2.

items.name: Remark 4.2.14: independence of lifts and dominance criterion
items.statement: (1) For α ∈ R and ν ∈ X_*(T), ⟨ν,α⟩ depends only on the image of ν in P^∨. Proposition 4.2.13 does not depend on the lifts of Ω: replacing ϖ by ϖ + γ and ϖ′ by ϖ′ + γ with γ ∈ X^*(G^ab) leaves ⟨μ,ϖ⟩ − ⟨λ,ϖ′⟩ unchanged, since μ − λ is a sum of coroots. (2) If μ, ν ∈ X_*(T)^+ with μ − ν ∈ X_*(T_sc), then μ − ν = Σ_i m_iα_i^∨ with m_i = ⟨μ − ν, ϖ_i⟩, so ν ≼ μ iff ⟨μ − ν, ϖ_i⟩ ≥ 0 for i = 1,…,n. Not every μ admits a set S as in Proposition 4.2.13; for example μ = (2,1,1) in type B_3 does not.
items.note: (2) is the criterion used in each case of the proof of Theorem 4.2.3 (R14–R18). Missing: routed to route 2.

items.name: Dynkin geodesics and the weights ϖ_α
items.statement: Assume G^ad simple. For α, α′ ∈ Δ, the geodesic from α to α′ is the unique sequence α = α_0, α_1, …, α_r = α′ of distinct simple roots with α_i and α_{i+1} adjacent. For ϖ ∈ Ω the fundamental weight of α′, put γ = 0 if r = 0 and γ = s_{α_1}⋯s_{α_{r−1}}α′ if r > 0, and ϖ_α := s_{α_1}⋯s_{α_r}ϖ = ϖ − γ. Then ⟨α^∨,ϖ_α⟩ > 0, so (ϖ,ϖ_α) ∈ 𝒲(−α). If ϖ is minuscule, then γ = Σ_{i=1}^r α_i.
items.locator: §4.2.17, p.39; last claim in the proof of Lemma 4.2.18
items.note: Input to Lemma 4.2.18, Corollary 4.2.19 (R20) and Propositions 4.3.9, 4.3.10. ϖ_α depends on ϖ; later notation writes ϖ_{n,α_i} and (ϖ_{n−1})_{α_i}. Missing: routed to route 2.

items.name: Conjugated root curves and the Cartan curve space 𝔗^cur_{λ,μ}
items.statement: For α ∈ Δ let H_α = dα^∨(1), so that (H_α, X_α, X_{−α}) is an 𝔰𝔩_2-triple. For 1 ≤ k ≤ k_α, u_{−α} = x_{−α}(1) lies in G(k[[t]]) ∩ t^λG(k[[t]])t^{−λ}, which fixes t^λ and acts on T_{t^λ}S_μ. Ad(u_{−α}) sends t^{⟨λ,α⟩−k}X_α to t^{⟨λ,α⟩−k}(X_α − H_α − X_{−α}) (printed with all plus signs). Taking T̃-weight components gives t^{⟨λ,α⟩−k}H_α ∈ T_{t^λ}S_μ. Conjugating the curve a ↦ t^λx_α(t^{−k}a) by u_{−α} shows that this vector lies in the span of smooth formal curves, because that span is T̃-stable. 𝔗^cur_{λ,μ} ⊂ 𝔗^tan_{λ,μ} is the span of these vectors. Equivalently (4.3.6): 𝔗^cur = ⊕_{α∈Δ} ⊕_{i=1}^{k_{−α}} t^{−i}k·H_α; the vectors with k ≤ ⟨λ,α⟩ vanish in T_{t^λ}Gr_G.
items.note: Needed to state Theorem 4.3.2 (R25). Missing: routed to route 4.

items.name: Proposition 4.3.4 (FM bound on Cartan directions)
items.statement: Let H ∈ 𝔱 and suppose t^{−l}H ∈ 𝔗^FM_{λ,μ} with l ≥ 1. Then 1 ≤ l ≤ l_H. In particular, for α ∈ Δ, k_{−α} ≤ l_{H_α}, since t^{⟨λ,α⟩−k_α}H_α = t^{−k_{−α}}H_α ∈ 𝔗^cur ⊂ 𝔗^FM.
items.locator: Proposition 4.3.4 and the following paragraph, p.41 (proof: 'a similar computation to Proposition 4.2.10')
items.note: There is no characteristic-p problem here: H acts on each weight space by the scalar dϖ′(H). The same k[ε]-computation proves the converse (t^{−l}H ∈ 𝔗^FM iff 1 ≤ l ≤ l_H). Remark 4.3.14 uses the converse without stating it. Missing: routed to route 4.

items.name: Weights of Weyl modules and minuscule modules (black box)
items.statement: For ν ∈ X^*(T)^+, V(ν) has the same weights as the characteristic-0 irreducible module of highest weight ν; this set is W-stable and saturated. The weights of V(−w_0ν) are the negatives of those of V(ν). If ϖ is minuscule, V(ϖ) is irreducible with weights W·ϖ, each of multiplicity 1, and whenever ϖ′ and ϖ′ + α are both weights, X_α maps the ϖ′-line isomorphically onto the (ϖ′+α)-line. In characteristic p, V(ν)^* ≅ H^0(−w_0ν), which is in general not isomorphic to V(−w_0ν).
items.locator: Used in §4.2.9, in the proofs of Propositions 4.2.10 and 4.2.13 and Lemma 4.2.18 (pp.35–39); cf. [Ja03, II]
items.note: R08 records V(ν) but not these properties, on which E9 and its repair depend. Missing: routed to route 3.

items.name: Special fibre of local models for Res_{O_K/O_F}H with H split (black box)
items.statement: Let 𝒢 = Res_{O_K/O_F}H with H split reductive over O_K, H^ad simple, and p ∤ |π_1(G^der)|. Let K_0 ⊂ K be the maximal unramified subextension of F, with residue field k_0. Then M^loc_{𝒢,μ} ⊗_{O_E} k (= M_{𝒢,μ} ⊗ k by Theorem 3.2.15, built from a Beilinson–Drinfeld Grassmannian as in Definition 3.2.6 and [Le16, §3.3]) is identified with the affine Schubert variety S_μ̲ ⊂ Gr_G̲. Here G̲ = ∏_{φ:k_0→k} H ⊗ k and μ̲_φ = Σ_{θ:K→K̄ inducing φ} μ_θ.
items.note: The text calls this 'a case of unpacking the constructions in [Le16] and above' and gives no proof of the identification with a single Schubert variety. The introduction (§1.2.2, p.6) speaks of a union of Schubert varieties, while Remark 4.1.3 and Lemma 4.4.2 identify the special fibre with a single one. Missing: routed to route 4.

items.name: Minuscule components of abelian-type pairs for Weil restrictions (cited)
items.statement: If (G,{μ}) is of abelian type and G_{K̄} ≅ ∏_{θ:K→K̄} H_{K̄}, then every μ_θ^ad is minuscule. If H is of type D_n, then either μ_θ^ad ∈ {ϖ_1^∨, 1} for all θ or μ_θ^ad ∈ {ϖ_{n−1}^∨, ϖ_n^∨, 1} for all θ.
items.locator: Proof of Lemma 4.4.2, p.47, cited as [PR26, Prop. 7.2.1] and its proof
items.note: Printed with weights ϖ_i for the coweights ϖ_i^∨. This is what makes (G̲, μ̲) of mod p abelian type, in the dominant reading of Definition 4.1.2. Missing: routed to route 4.

items.name: Pairs over D_R and base change of M̃_1
items.statement: Let R be a Noetherian complete local ring with residue field k. Pairs (M,M_1) over D_R are the same as pairs consisting of a finite free Ŵ(R)-module M of rank n and a submodule M_1 ⊂ M with M/M_1 a finite free R-module of rank n−d. For such a pair, M = L⊕T and M_1 = L⊕Î_R T with L, T finite free of ranks d and n−d [Lau14, 2.C]. The functor (M,M_1) ↦ M̃_1 generalizes [KP18, §3.1]. A local homomorphism R' → R of such rings induces D_{R'} → D_R and base change of pairs [KP18, 3.1.6], and there are natural isomorphisms M̃_{Ŵ(R),1} ≅ M̃'_{Ŵ(R'),1} ⊗_{Ŵ(R')} Ŵ(R) (5.1.6). In particular, if (M_0,M_{0,1}) is the base change along R → k, then M̃_{0,1} ≅ M̃_1 ⊗_{Ŵ(R)} W(k).
items.note: §5.2.1 uses this when it says that (M,M_1) defined by the universal filtration is a pair over Ŵ(R_E), and wherever M̃_{0,1} appears. Missing: routed to route 5.

items.name: Lemma 5.1.11 applies to D_B → D_{B/k} (Remark 5.1.13)
items.statement: Let B be an Artin local k-algebra with m_B² = 0 and residue field k. Lemma 5.1.11 applies to F = D_B, with the natural morphisms D_B → D_k and D_k → D_B. Then I' = Î_{B/k} = Î_B ⊕ [m_B], and α: F → F' is the natural frame morphism D_B → D_{B/k} (m_B with trivial divided powers). Lemma 5.1.9 also applies to D_B → D_{B/k} for any Artin local B with m_B² = 0 and residue field k.
items.locator: Remark 5.1.13, p. 51; note after Lemma 5.1.9, p. 50
items.note: This is used to define c in Lemma 5.1.15 (B = R/𝔞), in (5.2.2) (B = R_G/𝔞_G) and for D_{k[ε]} in Prop. 5.3.11. Missing: routed to route 5.

items.name: Ψ constant modulo 𝔞 (corrected)
items.statement: Let R be as in §5.1 with Ŵ(R) p-torsion free, 𝔞 = m² + pR, and M = M_0⊗_{W(k)}Ŵ(R) fixed as in §5.1.14. Let (M,M_1,Φ,Φ_1) be a Dieudonné display over Ŵ(R) with triple (M,M̃_1,Ψ), and (M_0,M̃_{0,1},Ψ_0) its base change to k. Ψ is constant modulo 𝔞 if the composite M̃_{0,1}⊗_{W(k)}Ŵ(R/𝔞) →^{c} M̃_1⊗_{Ŵ(R)}Ŵ(R/𝔞) →^{Ψ} M⊗_{Ŵ(R)}Ŵ(R/𝔞) = M_0⊗_{W(k)}Ŵ(R/𝔞) equals Ψ_0⊗1, where c is the connection isomorphism of Lemma 5.1.15.
items.note: This replaces [KP18, 3.1.1] and is the hypothesis of the corrected [KP18, Lem. 3.1.12] (F11). F11 folds it into a hypothesis without defining it. Missing: routed to route 5.

items.name: Tensors horizontal at x, and descent of c to c^𝒢
items.statement: In the setting of §5.2.1 (𝒪 = Z_p), let 𝔞_G = m_G² + π_E R_G ⊂ R_G. By Lemma 5.1.15 there is a canonical isomorphism c: M̃_{0,1}⊗_{W(k)}Ŵ(R_G/𝔞_G) ≅ M̃_1⊗_{Ŵ(R_G)}Ŵ(R_G/𝔞_G) (5.2.2). The tensors s̃_a are horizontal at x if c(s̃_{a,0}⊗1) = s̃_a⊗1, where M̃_{0,1} = Im(φ*M_{0,1} → φ*M_0). If this holds for a finite set (s_a) cutting out 𝒢 ↪ GL(Λ), then c descends uniquely to an isomorphism of 𝒢-torsors c^𝒢: T_0⊗_{W(k)}Ŵ(R_G/𝔞_G) ≅ T⊗_{Ŵ(R_G)}Ŵ(R_G/𝔞_G).
items.note: F15 builds this in, but the definition itself and the c^𝒢 construction, which Def. 5.2.5 calls 'as above', have no item. Here 𝔞 ⊂ 𝔞_G, so c is the base change of Lemma 5.1.15's c. Missing: routed to route 5.

items.name: Very good embedding into GL(ℒ) for a periodic lattice chain
items.statement: Let GL(ℒ) be the parahoric group scheme of a periodic lattice chain ℒ in V. A good integral Hodge embedding (𝒢,μ) ↪ (GL(ℒ),μ_d) is very good if the good integral Hodge embedding (𝒢,μ) ↪ (GL(tot(ℒ)),μ_{rd}), obtained by composing with the diagonal, is very good in the sense of Def. 5.2.5. Here tot(ℒ) is the direct sum of the r lattices of a determining segment (§3.4.3).
items.note: F33 covers only the independence statement. Theorem 6.1.1 is phrased with this notion. Missing: routed to route 5.

items.name: Very good embeddings over unramified 𝒪
items.statement: Suppose 𝒪 ≅ W(F_q) is finite unramified over Z_p. The definitions extend: the arguments of [KP18, §3.2] give φ*(s_a⊗1) ∈ M̃_1^⊗, and a good integral Hodge embedding is called very good (at x) when the φ*(s_a⊗1) are horizontal.
items.note: This is needed to make sense of Lemma 5.2.7 (F17). F13 mentions unramified 𝒪 but does not give the definition. Missing: routed to route 5.

items.name: Existence of tensors cutting out 𝒢 (cited)
items.statement: For the local model triple and good integral Hodge embedding 𝒢 ↪ GL(Λ) of §5.2.1, there is a set of tensors (s_a) ⊂ Λ^⊗ = ⊕_{m,n}Λ^{⊗m}⊗(Λ^∨)^{⊗n} that cuts out 𝒢 in GL(Λ) scheme-theoretically over all 𝒪-algebras. Cited as [KP18, Prop. 1.3.2] and [P23, 3.2.1].
items.note: A black box. Its exact hypotheses are in the cited sources. Reviewer check: the paper's Λ^⊗ has no symmetric or exterior powers, whereas (from memory) KP18 §1.3 allows them. [P23, 3.2.1] may be the source that matches this narrower Λ^⊗. Missing: routed to route 5.

items.name: 𝒢-fixed endomorphisms preserve the universal filtration (cited)
items.statement: If t: Λ → Λ is an endomorphism fixed by 𝒢, then t(ℱ) ⊂ ℱ for the universal filtration ℱ of Gr(d,Λ) restricted to M^loc_{𝒢,μ}. It suffices to check this on the generic fibre, where it follows from [KP18, 3.2.5].
items.note: A black-box input to Lemma 5.3.2 (F18). Missing: routed to route 5.

items.name: Zink logarithmic coordinates on square-zero ideals (cited)
items.statement: Let S be an Artin local ring with residue field k, and 𝔍 ⊂ S an ideal with 𝔍² = 0, equipped with trivial divided powers. Zink's logarithmic coordinates give a functorial decomposition Ŵ(𝔍) = I_{Ŵ(𝔍)} ⊕ [𝔍] (so Î_{S/k} = Î_S ⊕ [m_S] when 𝔍 = m_S) and Ŵ(𝔍) ≅ ⊕_{m≥0} 𝔍. Ŵ(𝔍) is a square-zero ideal of Ŵ(S). If S has characteristic p, then p·Ŵ(𝔍) = 0 and φ(Ŵ(𝔍)) = 0.
items.locator: §5.1.1 b) (p. 48); proof of Lemma 5.1.15 (p. 52); proof of Prop. 5.3.11 (p. 60); proof of Prop. 5.3.20 (p. 62)
items.note: [Zi02, Lemma 38], [Lau14, 2.C, 2.D]. Used as a black box in (5.1.18), in the final step of Prop. 5.3.11, and in the kernel equality of Prop. 5.3.20. Missing: routed to route 5.

items.name: KP18 Cor. 3.2.11 for a disconnected 𝒢
items.statement: In the setting of §5.3.19, with (s_a) cutting out 𝒢: s̃_a ∈ M̃_1^⊗ over Ŵ(R_{G^0}), and the 𝒢-scheme T' of isomorphisms M̃_1 ≅ Λ taking s̃_a to s_a is a 𝒢-torsor. Since the coweight lies in G°, the 𝒢-scheme Isom_{(s_a)}(F, M_𝔖)|_{D^*} of [KP18, proof of Lem. 3.2.6] is induced from a trivial 𝒢^0-torsor, so [KP18, Lem. 3.2.6] holds. Hence T' ≅ T^0 ×^{𝒢^0} 𝒢, where T^0 is the 𝒢^0-torsor of (𝒢^0,μ°).
items.note: An adaptation of cited results. Prop. 5.3.20 is used in §6 (pp. 70, 83), so this step is on the path to the main results. Missing: routed to route 5.

items.name: Types excluded by Theorem 6.1.1: D_n^H and exceptional A_n (simple adjoint case)
items.statement: Suppose G^ad is simple over Q_p. The assumptions of Theorem 6.1.1 exclude two cases. (1) Type D_n^H, n ≥ 4: G^ad = Res_{F/Q_p}H^ad with H^ad ⊗_F Q̄_p ≅ PSO_{2n} and μ^ad ≠ 1, such that for each φ : F → Q̄_p the component μ^ad_φ : G_{m,Q̄_p} → H^ad ⊗_F Q̄_p ≅ PSO_{2n} is of type ϖ_n^∨ or ϖ_{n−1}^∨, or is trivial. (2) Type A_n with adjoint group G^ad = Res_{F/Q_p}PGL_m(D), where D is a division F-algebra whose index is divisible by p. These cases are handled by explicit PEL-type Hodge embeddings (§§6.2–6.3).
items.note: This is the concrete form of (NE) for non-split groups. §6.2.2 refers back to it ('of type D_n^H, as above'). For n = 4 the distinction between ϖ_1^∨ and ϖ_3^∨, ϖ_4^∨ depends on the chosen identification with PSO_8 (triality); the text does not discuss this. Missing: routed to route 5.

items.name: Local models are invariant under maps inducing isomorphisms on adjoint groups (cited)
items.statement: Let (G,{μ},𝒢) → (G',{μ'},𝒢') be a morphism of local model triples over Q_p such that G → G' induces an isomorphism G^ad ≅ G'^ad, with 𝒢 and 𝒢' attached to the same point of the (common reduced) building. Then it induces an isomorphism of local models M^loc_{𝒢,μ} ≅ M^loc_{𝒢',μ'} ⊗_{O_{E'}} O_E. [SW20, Prop. 21.5.1], [HPR20, Prop. 2.14(c)]
items.locator: Proof of Theorem 6.1.1, p. 65 (also used in §3.4.2, p. 28, and §7.2, p. 76); also §3.4.2, p. 28
items.note: Used as a black box. In the proof of 6.1.1 it is applied twice: to 𝒢 → 𝒢', and to Res_{Z̃_p/Z_p}𝒢̃ → Res_{Z̃_p/Z_p}𝒢̃'. SW20 proves it for v-sheaves; passing to the normal scheme models needs the full-faithfulness step (Proposition 3.4.1). No existing item states it. Missing: routed to route 4.

items.name: Γ-stable lattice Λ̃ and descended chain L in the proof of Theorem 6.1.1
items.statement: In the setting of Theorem 6.1.1, fix embeddings F_i ↪ Q̄_p. Apply Lemma 6.1.2 and Proposition 2.2.2 to each H_i, moving x inside its facet without changing 𝒢. This gives a finite tame Galois extension Q̃_p/Q_p with the following properties: Q̃_p contains the maximal tame subextension of each F_i/Q_p; H_i splits over F̃_i := F_iQ̃_p; and each x̄_i ∈ B(H_i^der,F_i) is hyperspecial in B(H_i^der,F̃_i). Let Γ = Gal(Q̃_p/Q_p) and Γ_i = Gal(F̃_i/F_i) ⊂ Γ, so that F_i ⊗ Q̃_p ≅ ∏_{Γ/Γ_i}F̃_i. Then 𝒢 = (Res_{Z̃_p/Z_p}𝒢̃)^Γ with 𝒢̃ = 𝒢̃_x, and 𝒢̃' ≅ ∏_i∏_{γ∈Γ/Γ_i}Res_{Õ_i/Z̃_p}H̃_i, with H̃_i reductive over Õ_i = O_{F̃_i}. The maps 𝒢 → 𝒢' and 𝒢̃ → 𝒢̃' are closed immersions (Proposition 2.1.5(3)). Proposition 2.4.2 gives Γ_i-stable Õ_i-lattices Λ̃_i ⊂ W_i ⊗_{F_i}F̃_i with closed immersions H̃_i ↪ GL(Λ̃_i). Put Λ̃ := ⊕_i⊕_{γ∈Γ/Γ_i}Λ̃_i. This is a Γ-stable Z̃_p-lattice in V ⊗ Q̃_p, and it gives closed immersions (6.1.3) 𝒢̃' ↪ GL(Λ̃) and (6.1.4) 𝒢 ↪ Res𝒢̃ ↪ Res𝒢̃' ↪ Res GL(Λ̃) ↪ GL(Λ̃), with Λ̃ viewed as a Z_p-lattice. In (6.1.4), 𝒢 is cut out in Res𝒢̃ ↪ GL(Λ̃) by Z_p-linear endomorphisms of Λ̃. Finally L := {(π̃^iΛ̃)^Γ}_{i∈Z} is a chain in V = (V ⊗ Q̃_p)^Γ (Lemma 2.3.3), Λ := tot(L) ⊂ V^{⊕r}, and after an unramified extension 𝒢 ↪ GL(Λ) is a direct summand of 𝒢 ↪ GL(Λ̃) (see (2.3.8)); see diagram (6.1.7).
items.note: Theorem 6.1.9, Theorem 6.2.3 and Corollaries 6.2.10 and 6.3.5 reuse this construction by quoting 'the argument in the proof of Theorem 6.1.1'. Formalizing any of them needs it as a separate object. Missing: routed to route 5.

items.name: Duals of Γ-invariant lattices under tame descent
items.statement: Let Q̃_p/Q_p be finite, tame and Galois with group Γ and uniformizer π̃, and let δ generate its different. Let ψ be a perfect Q_p-bilinear form on V, extended Q̃_p-bilinearly. For a Γ-stable Z̃_p-lattice M ⊂ V ⊗ Q̃_p, write M^∨ = {v : ψ(v,M) ⊂ Z̃_p}. Then the Z_p-dual of M^Γ in V is (δ^{-1}M^∨)^Γ. In particular ((π̃^mΛ̃)^Γ)^∨ = (π̃^{−m}δ^{-1}Λ̃^∨)^Γ, so the dual chain of {(π̃^iΛ̃)^Γ} is {(π̃^iΛ̃^∨)^Γ}. The same holds for a tame Galois extension K̃/K with O_K-lattices and a K-valued form.
items.locator: Proof of Theorem 6.1.9, p. 66; used implicitly for self-duality in the proof of Theorem 6.2.3, p. 69
items.note: Asserted without proof, but true. For x ∈ (M^Γ)^∨: Tr(M) ⊂ M^Γ gives Tr ψ(x,M) ⊂ Z_p. Conversely, δ^{-1}Z̃_p ∩ Q_p = Z_p because v_p(δ) < 1 for tame extensions. The different δ matters here; see the sourceIssue on Theorem 6.1.9. Missing: routed to route 5.

items.name: Adjoint groups of type D_n^H are orthogonal or quaternionic unitary (cited)
items.statement: Suppose G^ad is simple over Q_p and (G^ad,μ^ad) is of type D_n^H. Then G^ad ≅ Res_{K/Q_p}G'^ad for a finite extension K/Q_p, where either (a) G' = GO^+(V,h) for V ≅ K^{2n} with a perfect symmetric K-bilinear form h, or (b) G' = GU^+(T,φ) for a left D-module T ≅ D^n over a quaternion division K-algebra D, with a nondegenerate quaternionic antihermitian form φ for the main involution. [PZ13, §5.3.8], [Gr12]
items.note: Black-box classification on which all of §6.2 rests. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Hyperspecial stabilizers of split GO^+ are stabilizers of self-dual lattices (cited)
items.statement: Let K̃/K be tame Galois with group Γ, and suppose G' = GO^+(V,h) splits over K̃. If the stabilizer of a Γ-fixed point x ∈ B(G',K̃) is hyperspecial, it is the stabilizer of a Γ-stable Õ-lattice Λ̃ ⊂ V ⊗_K K̃ that is self-dual up to homothety for h_{K̃}, i.e. Λ̃^∨ = π̃^aΛ̃. After adjoining a square root of π̃ to K̃ (and passing to a Galois closure, still tame since p > 2), Λ̃ can be rescaled so that Λ̃^∨ = Λ̃, and the stabilizer is 𝒢̃' = GO^+(Λ̃,h). [BT87], [KaP23, 15.2]
items.note: Cited input. The rescaling step is correct: (π̃^{a/2}Λ̃)^∨ = π̃^{a/2}Λ̃. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: (6.2.5): GO(Λ̃,h) as a scheme-theoretic intersection (cited)
items.statement: Let Λ̃ be a self-dual Õ-lattice for h and M̃ := O^2 ⊗_O Λ̃ ⊂ W_{K̃} = V_{K̃} ⊕ V_{K̃}, with ψ = S ⊗ h and S the standard alternating form on O^2. Then GO(Λ̃,h) = GL_{End_O(O^2)}(M̃) ∩ GSp(M̃,ψ) as a scheme-theoretic intersection. Hence Res_{Õ/Z_p}GO(Λ̃) is cut out in Res_{Õ/Z_p}GSp(M̃) by endomorphisms of M̃. [RZ96, App. to Ch. 3, case (II), Prop. A.18, A.19]
items.note: Numbered display, and a key input for the proof of Theorem 6.2.3. It can also be checked directly via Morita equivalence over Õ. Missing: routed to route 5.

items.name: Quaternionic hermitian forms over a p-adic field are standard (cited)
items.statement: Let D be a quaternion division algebra over the p-adic field K with its main involution. Every nondegenerate quaternionic hermitian form S on a right D-module T_0 ≅ D^s has a D-basis in which S((d_i),(d'_i)) = Σ_{i=1}^s d̄_i d'_i. [Sh73]
items.note: Used to reduce σ_{T_0} to s copies of σ_D. It follows because Nrd : D^× → K^× is onto. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Buildings and stabilizers of GL_m(D) via O_D-lattice chains (cited)
items.statement: Let A^* = Res_{K/Q_p}GL_m(D) with D a central division K-algebra, and V = D^m. Points x ∈ B(A^*,Q_p) correspond to graded periodic right O_D-lattice chains (L,c) in V [BT84]. The stabilizer group scheme 𝒢_x is the group scheme of O_D-automorphisms of the chain L [BT84, 3.6, Thm].
items.note: Black box behind Proposition 6.3.2 and Corollary 6.3.5. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Fundamental Hodge embedding
items.statement: Let (G,X) be of Hodge type with G^ad simple, satisfying (†): G^c ≅ Res_{F/Q}H^c. A Hodge embedding ι: (G,X) → (GSp(V),S^±) is fundamental if V has the structure of an F-vector space such that ι|_{G^c} factors as Res_{F/Q}H^c → Res_{F/Q}GL_F(V) → GL(V). The first map must be the Weil restriction of a morphism of F-group schemes H^c → GL_F(V); the second is restriction of structure (GL_F(V) = F-linear automorphisms).
items.note: Hypothesis of Lemma 7.2.8 and of Propositions 7.2.10(3) and 7.2.16. The claim right after the definition, that V ⊗_Q F always gives a fundamental embedding, is false (new source issue). Missing: routed to route 8.

items.name: The groups H′ and G′ attached to a fundamental Hodge embedding
items.statement: Given a fundamental Hodge embedding, H′ ⊂ GL_F(V) is the subgroup generated by H^c and the homotheties F^×, and G′ := Res_{F/Q}H′. Then G ⊂ G′, and G → GSp(V) extends to G′ → GL(V), obtained by restriction of structure from an F-morphism H′ → GL_F(V). For the Hodge-type liftings of §7.2.3 these H′, G′ coincide with the ones defined there.
items.note: Used in Lemma 7.2.8 and in the proofs of Propositions 7.2.10 and 7.2.16 (G′_i := Res_{F_i/Q_p}H′_{F_i}). Missing: routed to route 8.

items.name: Deligne's Hodge-type lifting of an abelian-type datum
items.statement: Take S, W, K_S, K, T as in §7.2.2–7.2.3 (item S15) and let V := W ⊗_F K, viewed as a Q-vector space. Let G″ ⊂ GL(V) be generated by K_S^×, Res_{F/Q}H^♯ and K^× (Deligne's G_3), and G′ ⊂ G″ be generated by Res_{F/Q}H^♯, F^× and the maximal compact subtorus of Z_{G″}. Then G′ = Res_{F/Q}H′ with H′ tamely ramified at all places above p, and G′ → GL(V) comes from an F-morphism H′ → GL_F(W ⊗_F K). V carries a Hodge structure of type (0,−1),(−1,0) from some h′: S → G′_R, and [De79, Cor. 2.3.3] gives a Shimura datum (G,X) with G ⊂ G′, an alternating form ψ on V and a Hodge embedding (G,X) → (GSp(V),S^±). G is generated by G′^der = Res_{F/Q}H^♯, the maximal compact subtorus of Z_{G′} and the scalars G_m; equivalently G = (G′ ∩ GSp(V))^0. These data satisfy (†) and the Hodge embedding is fundamental.
items.note: S15 covers only the choice of S, K, T. The tameness of H′ at p uses p > 2: the splitting fields have degree ≤ 2 and triality forms are excluded. Missing: routed to route 8.

items.name: Adaptedness criterion for the versal p-divisible group
items.statement: Under (A), (B), (C), let x ∈ S_K(G,X)(k) and let 𝒢 be the versal p-divisible group over Spf R_E built in the proof of Theorem 7.1.3. For K/Q̆_p finite, a local homomorphism u: R_E → O_K (printed 'u: R → O_K') factors through R_G if and only if 𝒢_u is (𝒢,μ_h)-adapted in the sense of [KZ25, Def. 3.2.4] (cf. [PR26, §7.1]).
items.note: The input from which Proposition 7.1.6 (item S07) follows. Its proof uses [KP18, Prop. 2.3.17]; cf. [KZ25, Prop. 4.1.9]. Missing: routed to route 5.

items.name: Smooth Z_(p)-models of G and G^ad under (E)
items.statement: In the setting of §7.1.12 under (A)–(E), let G°_{Z(p)} (resp. G^{ad,○}_{Z(p)}) be the Z_(p)-model of G (resp. G^ad) attached to 𝒢° (resp. 𝒢^{ad,○}) as in [KP18, §4.6.1], and let Z_{Z(p)} be the closure of Z_G in G°_{Z(p)}. R-smoothness of the torus Z_G and descent imply that Z_{Z(p)} and G^{ad,○}_{Z(p)} are smooth, and that the p-adic completion of G^{ad,○}_{Z(p)} is the parahoric group scheme of G^ad attached to x^ad. This is the analogue of [KP18, Lem. 4.6.2(2)].
items.note: This is the only place where (E) enters Proposition 7.1.14. Missing: routed to route 8.

items.name: Local models of a Hodge-type lifting and of the abelian-type datum agree
items.statement: In the setting of §7.1.12 there is an equivariant isomorphism M^loc_{𝒢,μ_h} ⊗_{O_E} O_{E′} ≅ M^loc_{𝒢_2°,μ_{h_2}} ⊗_{O_{E_2}} O_{E′}. It comes from the isomorphisms of local-model v-sheaves induced by G_2 → G_2^ad and G → G^ad ≅ G_2^ad ([SW20, Prop. 21.5.1]) together with full faithfulness of the diamond functor on these normal flat models ([SW20, Prop. 18.4.1]).
items.note: Black box [SW20, Prop. 21.5.1]; the same input is used in §6.1 (p.66) and §4. Missing: routed to route 8.

items.name: Centre modifications of the Hodge-type lifting (NE case)
items.statement: Choose a maximal F-torus S′ ⊂ H′ such that T′ = Res_{F/Q}S′ ⊂ G′ contains the image of some h ∈ X and S′_{F_i} is H′_i(F_i)-conjugate to the centralizer S′_i of a maximal F̆_i-split torus of H′_i := H′_{F_i}. Put T = G ∩ T′, a maximal torus of G whose maximal compact subtorus T_0 = Res_{F/Q}S_0 is quasi-tame at p. Set G_1 = G ×^{Z_G} T, with X_1 induced by h × 1. Then (G_1,X_1) is of Hodge type and satisfies (1), (2) and (†), with G_1^c = G^c ×^{Z_{G,0}} T_0, Z_{G_1} = T and Z^c_{G_1} = T_0 quasi-tame. A further modification (G × T′ × T″)/(Z_{G^der} × Z_{G,0}) as in [KP18, Lem. 4.6.22], with T′, T″ Weil restrictions of F-tori that are quasi-tame over Q_p, makes X_*(Z^c_G/Z_{G^der})_I torsion free and keeps (†).
items.note: The Hodge property of the modified data comes from [KP18, Lem. 4.6.22] (Hodge embedding W = Hom_{Z_G}(V,V)). The paper does not show these embeddings are fundamental (new source issue). The symbol T′ is used both for Res S′ and for one of the tori in the second modification. Missing: routed to route 8.

items.name: Choice of a maximal torus with prescribed local conjugacy class ([Ki10, Prop. 2.2.4])
items.statement: (Cited, 'arguing as in'.) Given H′ over F and, for each prime 𝔭_i | p of F, the centralizer S′_i ⊂ H′_{F_i} of a maximal F̆_i-split torus, there is a maximal F-torus S′ ⊂ H′ such that T′ = Res_{F/Q}S′ contains the image of some h ∈ X and S′_{F_i} is H′_{F_i}(F_i)-conjugate to S′_i for all i.
items.locator: Proof of Proposition 7.2.10, p.80, citing [Ki10, Prop. 2.2.4]
items.note: Black box. It needs weak approximation on the variety of maximal tori together with the real condition. Missing: routed to route 8.

items.name: Shape of the invariant alternating forms in the exceptional cases ([Sa67])
items.statement: (Cited.) In the proof of Proposition 7.2.16, the H′_{F_i}-invariant alternating F_i-forms Ψ_i on V_i have the form considered in §6.2.2 in type D^H ([Sa67, 2.2]) and the form of §6.3.4 in type A ([Sa67, 2.1]).
items.note: Needed to apply Corollary 6.2.10 and Corollary 6.3.5. Missing: routed to route 8.

items.name: v-sheaf of the completion equals the formal completion of the 𝒢-shtuka moduli
items.statement: (Cited.) For S_K(G,X) as in Theorem 7.1.8 and x ∈ S_K(G,X)(k), the v-sheaf attached to Ô_{S_K(G,X),x} is isomorphic to the 'formal completion' at the corresponding point of the integral moduli of 𝒢-shtukas. This is [PR24, Thm. 1.3.2(c)] when 𝒢 is parahoric, and [DvHKZ, Thm. 4.2.3] and its proof for general stabilizers.
items.note: It is combined with [PR26, Thm. 2.5.5] (I04) and [SW20, Prop. 18.4.1]. I02/I03 describe the canonical-model framework but not this specific statement. Missing: routed to route 7.

items.name: Parahoric local model diagram (7.2.25) for the Hodge-type lifting
items.statement: For (G,X) as in Proposition 7.2.19, pulling back the diagram of Theorem 7.1.3 to S_{K°_p}(G,X) gives a 𝒢-equivariant local model diagram. By [DvHKZ, Prop. 4.3.3] its 𝒢-torsor reduces to a 𝒢°-torsor. This gives (7.2.25): π°: S̃_{K°_p}(G,X) → S_{K°_p}(G,X), a 𝒢°-torsor, and a 𝒢°-equivariant smooth q°: S̃_{K°_p}(G,X) → M^loc_{𝒢°,μ_h}. The construction of Proposition 7.1.14 applied to (7.2.25) gives the 𝒢^{ad,○}-torsor of Corollary 7.2.24.
items.note: The top vertex is printed S̃^ad_{K°_p}(G,X), although this is a 𝒢°-torsor (misprint). Missing: routed to route 8.

items.name: Néron–Ogg–Shafarevich criterion
items.statement: (Cited, unnamed reference.) An abelian variety over the fraction field of a discrete valuation ring R has good reduction if and only if its ℓ-adic Tate module is unramified for some (equivalently every) prime ℓ different from the residue characteristic. With the prime-to-p level structure of the pro-variety, this extends R[1/p]-points of Sh_{K_p}(G,X) to R-points of the Siegel model, hence of S_{K_p}(G,X), R being normal.
items.note: It gives the extension property (item S04) and hence Proposition 7.1.14(1) and Theorem 7.2.21(1). Planned: NeronModelsAndSemistableAbelianVarieties R11.5 plans the Néron–Ogg–Shafarevich criterion.

items.name: Arguments of [KP18, §4.3–§4.6] used 'verbatim'
items.statement: (Cited proofs.) Given Theorem 7.1.3 in place of [KP18, Thm. 4.2.7], the arguments of [KP18, §4.3] (Prop. 4.3.9, using (4.3.4) = assumption (D)) prove Proposition 7.1.11. Those of [KP18, §§4.4–4.6] (up to Cor. 4.6.18, with the correction §7.3.1(3) to Lemma 4.6.13 and Cor. 4.6.15) prove Proposition 7.1.14. The argument in the proof of [KP18, Thm. 4.6.23] gives, when X_*(G^ab)_I is torsion free, a point x lifting x^ad with 𝒢 = 𝒢° (Theorem 7.2.21).
items.locator: §7.1.10 (Proposition 7.1.11), proof of Proposition 7.1.14 (p.76), proof of Theorem 7.2.21 (p.85)
items.note: These proofs are given by reference. They must be read with the corrected inputs (E1–E5). Missing: routed to route 8.

items.name: Stabilizer group scheme lifting 𝒢_2; the fields E′ and levels K_{2,p}, K°_{2,p}
items.statement: Let (G_2,X_2) carry a central isogeny α: G^der → G_2^der inducing (G^ad,X^ad) ≅ (G_2^ad,X_2^ad). Let x^ad be the image of x in B(G^ad,Q_p), fix x_2 ∈ B(G_2,Q_p) lifting x^ad, and let 𝒢_2 (resp. 𝒢_2°) be its stabilizer (resp. parahoric). One says that 𝒢 lifts 𝒢_2. Set K_{2,p} = 𝒢_2(Z_p), K°_{2,p} = 𝒢_2°(Z_p), and E′ = E·E_2, completed at a place v′ | v.
items.note: Used in Propositions 7.1.14, 7.2.10(3), 7.2.19(4) and Theorem 7.2.21. S12 covers only 𝒢^ad. Missing: routed to route 8.

routes.reason: The existing continuation owns integral Weil restriction, buildings and smooth parahoric/fixer models. Add quasi-tame and R-smooth inputs, tame fixed-point and stable-chain statements, the GO/GO+ distinction and smooth center/multiplier intersections here. No new copy of Bruhat–Tits theory is proposed.

routes.title: Root systems, Weyl groups, and the Cartan-Killing classification, Part II: dominant subtraction and Demazure reduction
routes.brief: Continue the candidate already proposed by PAPER-HE-21. Import root data, integral pairings, Weyl actions, dominant representatives and numbered classical types from Root systems, Weyl groups, and the Cartan–Killing classification (tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/RepresentationTheory/RootSystems). Import group root vectors and their modular representation action from Reductive algebraic groups (tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ReductiveGroups) and the integral-representations continuation below. Add the integral-coroot order and mod-p abelian coweight families needed here, without replacing the cocharacter lattice by a rational vector space. Define minuscule weights, k_alpha, active-weight minima l_alpha and the Cartan bound l_H. Prove Proposition4.2.13 with its fixed coroot coset and dominance-detecting minuscule set, then the separate A,B,C,D-real,D-quaternionic cases. Prove the sign-sensitive geodesic formula of Lemma4.2.18, correcting Corollary4.2.19 to k_minus_alpha. Prove Propositions4.3.9 and4.3.10; the latter requires an end-wall condition. Compute the D4 example while making no claim about the unknown actual Schubert tangent beyond the proved bounds. Keep the spin weight lattice and D end-root convention explicit. The Kisin–Zhou candidate RootSystemsDominancePartII overlaps this earlier direction: consolidate its dominant-coroot/Stembridge lane into this candidate at design intake, retaining both papers’ stable item ids and the additional Frobenius-orbit proof obligation. Do not build two dominance orders. Tests include A1 parity and the unequal signed bounds, half-integral B spin weights, the D last-root pairing, the D4 bound3 versus2, and failure of the test-set property for the source’s B example mu=(2,1,1). Corrections the design must carry: 'sum of minuscule coweights' in Definition 4.1.2(1) means a sum of dominant minuscule coweights (E39); the proof of Proposition 4.3.10 misses the case ϖ = ϖ_{n−1} or ϖ_n with α = α_j, j ≤ n−4, which the proof's own minimality argument covers (E48); and in §4.2.9 𝒲(α) must be read through weights (ϖ′ and ϖ′+α weights of V(ϖ)): the 'Equivalently' description fails in characteristic p, and with it the symmetry used for Proposition 4.2.10(1) (E9).
routes.reason: An earlier HE21 continuation already owns integral dominance and related Weyl combinatorics. This extraction extends that candidate and records the later KZ25 alias for consolidation; it does not propose another parallel root roadmap.

routes.title: Reductive algebraic groups, Part II: integral highest weights and modular root actions
routes.brief: Build on Reductive algebraic groups (tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ReductiveGroups), specifically its representation/comodule dictionary, reductive groups, pinnings and integral Chevalley–Demazure root maps. Import the abstract root datum from tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/RepresentationTheory/RootSystems and the existing Kostant lattice and root-subgroup coordinate APIs at the pins. Construct Weyl modules V(nu)=Ind_B^G(-w0 nu)^* for arbitrary dominant characters over algebraically closed fields of positive characteristic, via a compatible integral construction. Export weight spaces, duality, root-operator matrices, base change and the exact active-weight criterion used by KPZ4.2.9. Prove that minuscule modules have the needed one-dimensional orbit weights and nonzero root arrows, and distinguish that restricted fact from the printed general adjacent-weight assertion, which must be checked against Jantzen before use. Establish the centralizer-conjugacy of stable lattices in minuscule characteristic-zero representations used in Proposition3.3.10. Tests must include SL2 in characteristic p, a root action with a coefficient killed by p, minuscule spin weights, and the lattice-centralizer comparison. Do not re-plan characteristic-zero Lie highest-weight theory or Young-symmetrizer GL_n modules: their field and Q-algebra hypotheses do not supply this task. This lane is distinct from ReductiveGroupsArithmeticPartII, which owns global tori, cohomological transfer and rational conjugacy, and from ReductiveGroupsPartII, which owns local buildings and integral fixers. Coordinate-to-abstract-group comparison remains an explicit theorem.
routes.reason: The upstream reductive group roadmap supplies group/comodule and pinned group-scheme foundations, but not these positive-characteristic Weyl-module statements. ClassicalGroups and LieHighestWeight are characteristic zero in the relevant stages; the arithmetic and local-group continuations have different targets.

routes.title: Geometric Satake over the Fargues–Fontaine curve, Part II: integral local models and tangent geometry
routes.brief: Extend the existing candidate from PAPER-KISIN-ZHOU-25, retaining its same-residue-field curve lane. Import Geometric Satake over the Fargues–Fontaine curve (GeometricSatakeAndFusion GS0 loop and Witt geometry), Global shtukas and function-field Langlands (GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglands GS.1), Reductive groups, Part II (ReductiveGroupsPartII RG2.0a,RG2.2,RG2.3), the dominance continuation and the integral diamond comparison continuation. Define local Hodge/abelian-type data, standard assumptions, the local-model v-sheaf, polynomial Beilinson–Drinfeld model, naive closure, auxiliary prime-to-p cover and normal integral representative as separate objects. Under p>2, local abelian type, essential tameness and classical type, prove the flat proper normal representative with reduced special fiber. Separate component Cohen–Macaulayness from the stronger whole-model input. Prove Theorem3.1.9’s normalization-of-image statement and the genuinely stronger good closed-embedding existence in3.3.25, retaining the possible change of quasi-parahoric and the generic-facet/index refinements. The proof order is3.3.25 then3.4.1 then3.2.15. Define curve-spanned tangent spaces and the FM lattice-bound scheme. Prove root tangent equality for every mod-p abelian type under p-prime derived fundamental group, Cartan equality for A/B/C/D-real and the specified D-quaternionic end walls, then Theorems4.1.6 and4.4.3. Minimal-stratum spanning includes D-quaternionic; all-point spanning does not. Do not infer FM reducedness or infer spanning for arbitrary normal singularities. Import representation theory rather than rebuilding Weyl modules. Tests include a GL_n hyperspecial Grassmannian, a central cocharacter, a nonclosed normalization map, root degrees and the corrected reducible tangent-cone example. Corrections the design must carry: the proof of Lemma 3.4.1 must show that the v-sheaf local model of 𝒢 is closed in the Beilinson–Drinfeld Grassmannian of GL(Λ) (a proper monomorphism is a closed immersion), not take it as a definition (E34); §3.4.5 and Proposition 3.4.6 need 'H of classical type', which the argument through Proposition 2.2.2 uses (E36); in Remark 3.4.7 the closed immersion 𝕄_{GL(𝓛)} → 𝕄_{GL(Λ̃)} comes from Propositions 3.3.7 and 3.3.20, not from the facts the Remark states (E38). In characteristic p the last step of the proof of Proposition 4.2.10(2) fails (E9): the design must either prove the bound from both inclusions of (4.2.7), for pairs realised in the Weyl module V(ϖ) and in H^0(ϖ), or use only the minuscule pairs, which already give Φ^cur = Φ^tan = Φ^FM and Theorem 4.2.3; the dualisation in Remark 4.2.8(3) holds only in characteristic 0 (E42).
routes.reason: The existing GS0 geometry stops before flat integral scheme recovery and these tangent/embedding theorems. The KZ25 candidate already opens this exact direction; current work fills its major KPZ supplier.

routes.title: Finite flat group schemes and integral p-adic Hodge theory, Part II: corrected displays and very-good embeddings
routes.brief: Continue the existing tensor-deformation and ordinary-lift candidate from PAPER-KISIN-ZHOU-25. Import Finite flat group schemes and integral p-adic Hodge theory (FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory R07.2,R07.4,R07.6), Witt and divided-power carriers at the pins, integral local models from GeometricSatakeLocalModelsPartII, and local fixer/lattice theory from ReductiveGroupsPartII. Define Zink’s coefficient subring, strict frames, normal-decomposable pairs, the free tilde functor and relative PD frames. Prove the block formula, functor composition, decomposition independence and base change. The natural map to Frobenius pullback is injective only over p-torsion-free rings. Construct the canonical connection using relative frames; its commutative square does not characterize it after reduction. Prove the corrected constant-first-order versality theorem with the contravariant display/p-divisible convention. Define integral stabilizer tensors, adapted deformations and very-goodness modulo m^2+pi_E. Prove tensor integrality and triviality through the precise Anschütz purity supplier, then tensor-family independence, endomorphism horizontality, summand descent, sums of isomorphic copies and products of separate groups. Prove Theorem5.3.11 by power-series frames, integral tensor comparison and injective cotangent detection. Establish the separate arithmetic-curve criterion and the smooth generic-neutral closure lemma. Prove Theorem6.1.1 and the paired trace-dual theorem6.1.9 under non-exceptional,R-smooth,p-prime and generic-facet hypotheses. Independently construct D-quaternionic PEL and p-divisible-index A representations and their self-dual very-good chains. General goodness implies very-goodness remains unproved. Preserve KZ’s separate ordinary Breuil–Kisin lift lane. Tests include torsion kernels, canonical versus arbitrary connection, multiplier compatibility, dual conventions, Morita handedness and the distinct exceptional-factor assumptions. Corrections the design must carry: the proof of Proposition 5.3.18 must identify the tilde modules and tensors along the non-strict maps out of the Breuil–Kisin pair, as in [KP18, (3.2.10)] (E60); Theorem 6.1.1 needs R-smoothness over the tame extension Q̃_p, not only over Q_p, or that hypothesis added (E61); in Theorem 6.1.9 the dual lattice is the ψ-dual Λ̃^∨, not Λ̃^* (E62); in §6.3.1 and Proposition 6.3.2 the contragredient embedding needs the cocharacter μ·z^{-1} to be a Hodge embedding (E69); and in Corollary 6.3.5 the chain is Λ_i ⊕ (Λ_{-i})^⊥, whose members are not individually self-dual (E71).
routes.reason: The existing candidate owns tensor displays and very-good deformations. KPZ supplies the corrected construction and existence proofs; ordinary classification in R07 is imported, not repeated.

routes.title: Pro-étale descent, diamonds and small v-stacks, Part II: recovery of integral models
routes.brief: Import Pro-étale descent, diamonds and small v-stacks (DiamondsAndVStacks D6) for the analytic diamond and site comparison, together with the perfectoid and v-descent foundations it names. The paper uses two results here. (1) Scholze–Weinstein, Berkeley Lectures, Proposition 18.4.1: the functor X ↦ X^◇ is fully faithful on flat normal O_E-schemes and formal schemes in its scope (item I01). The paper applies it to proper flat normal O_E-schemes, the local model and the Grassmannian Gr(d,Λ)_{O_E}, to obtain ρ_* in §3.1.9 (p. 17) and the uniqueness in Lemma 3.4.1 (p. 28), and again in the proof of Theorem 7.1.8 (p. 74). State it with Scholze–Weinstein's own hypotheses before applying it; the paper does not restate them. (2) For a flat projective O_E-scheme given as the Zariski closure of its generic fibre in Gr(d,Λ)_{O_E}, its v-sheaf is the v-sheaf closure of the generic fibre's (item diamond-of-flat-closure), used without reference in the proof of Lemma 3.4.1. That proof also needs the fact recorded as the gap E34: a proper monomorphism of small v-sheaves is a closed immersion, so that the v-sheaf local model of 𝒢 embeds in the Beilinson–Drinfeld Grassmannian of GL(Λ). Tests must distinguish a normal integral model from its special-fibre point set and from an infinitesimal thickening, and a v-sheaf closure from the v-sheaf of a closure that is not flat. DvHKZ's own proof inputs (its Lemmas A3.4 and A3.5 and the perfect-scheme full faithfulness of Scholze–Weinstein 18.3.1) are not used by this paper and belong to the design of route 7 if that design proves DvHKZ Proposition 4.3.3.
routes.reason: D6 explicitly concerns analytic diamonds and étale-category equivalence, and disclaims general full faithfulness. The38 prior paper extractions contain no candidate owning these normal integral recovery statements.

routes.title: Hecke correspondences and local shtuka cohomology, Part II: integral parahoric models and crystalline diagrams
routes.brief: Import Hecke correspondences and local shtuka cohomology (HeckeStacksAndLocalShtukas HS2) for 𝒢-shtukas and their integral moduli, integral diamond recovery from DiamondsAndVStacksIntegralPartII, corrected tensor displays from FiniteFlatGroupsWithTensorsPartII and integral local models from GeometricSatakeLocalModelsPartII. The paper itself uses only [PR24, Thm. 1.3.2], [DvHKZ, Thm. 4.2.3] (proof of Theorem 7.1.8, p. 74), [PR26, Thm. 2.5.5] (p. 74) and [DvHKZ, Prop. 4.3.3] (proof of Corollary 7.2.24, p. 85), together with the compatibility of the scheme-theoretic and crystalline local model diagrams that Prop. 4.3.3 needs (item I05); DvHKZ's Lemma 4.3.4, its Appendix A lemmas and the perfect-scheme full faithfulness below are inputs of those proofs, not statements of this paper. Define the canonical integral parahoric/quasi-parahoric model system with the actual axioms of PR24 and DvHKZ4.1.4. Prove the Hodge-type existence theorem DvHKZ4.2.3 and the integral local-shtuka formal-completion comparison PR26 Theorem2.5.5. That comparison consumes KPZ §§5–6 and cannot prove those earlier results. Establish relative prismatic Dieudonné compatibility and the crystalline local-model comparison of DvHKZ AppendixA3.3 with its self-dual/smooth Siegel base assumptions. Prove the exact small/big diamond component sequences of Lemma4.3.4, then Proposition4.3.3: a scheme local-model diagram compatible with the crystalline one reduces to a connected-parahoric torsor, still with a smooth map. Use perfect-scheme full faithfulness and étale topological invariance for the component section. Do not infer this reduction for an arbitrary smooth torsor diagram. Tests include the connected case, a nontrivial component quotient, the identity level map and a diagram lacking crystalline compatibility. The HE21 candidate HeckeStacksAndLocalShtukasPartIIAffineDeligneLusztig owns generic ADLV dimensions/cordiality, which is a distinct lane; import any shared generic objects instead of recreating them.
routes.reason: HS2 supplies generic Hecke-fiber moduli, not canonical integral parahoric systems. The earlier ADLV continuation has a different endpoint. This is the missing integral direction needed for the strict-henselian and all-case connected-diagram refinements.

routes.title: Complex Shimura varieties and canonical models, Part II: integral models and reduction
routes.brief: Extend the candidate already used by PAPER-KISIN-MADAPUSIPERA-SHIN-22 and PAPER-KISIN-ZHOU-25; retain its reduction,Honda–Tate and Frobenius lanes. Import Complex Shimura varieties and canonical models (ShimuraVarieties V1,V6,V8), Shimura data (ShimuraData), Siegel and PEL moduli problems (PELModuli M1,M2,M4), Abelian schemes and arithmetic moduli, AutomorphicBundles tensor comparisons, and the four integral continuations in this extraction. Construct the parahoric Siegel lattice-chain supplier, then the Hodge normalization at a full stabilizer. Under(A) generic-facet full stabilizer,(B) R-smooth and p-prime derived fundamental group,(C) a very-good lattice embedding, prove Theorem7.1.3: pro-level DVR extension, G-torsor smooth local-model diagram, and ordinary henselization comparison with the same finite residue field when G is connected. Keep7.1.8 separate: its weaker self-dual-chain stabilizer hypotheses yield strict henselizations through integral shtukas. Define C=ker(G_sc→G_der), condition(D) on H¹(Q,C), and the distinct R-smooth center condition(E). Prove finite étale connected-level normalization, unramified component descent and the derived-cover finite component map. Construct H-sharp, Deligne’s minuscule vertex data, CM scalar extension, compact-center enlargement, trace polarization and Zarhin self-dual lattice; the abelian-type hypothesis is essential. Prove Proposition7.2.19’s four outputs and conditional torsion-free coinvariants via the common-multiplier fiber product. Finally prove Theorem7.2.21 for EVERY abelian-type datum at p>2: finite étale away-p tower, pro-level DVR bijection, étale-local local-model geometry and the smooth adjoint quotient torsor diagram. Prove its elementary connected reduction under(NE), then Corollary7.2.24 in all cases using the compatible crystalline diagram. Apply every erratum in§7.3, especially conjugated component levels and the added very-good hypothesis. No duplicate generic canonical-model construction is allowed. Corrections the design must carry: the paragraph after Definition 7.2.7 (p. 78) is false, since V ⊗_Q F is never a fundamental Hodge embedding when F ≠ Q (E79); so the proof of Proposition 7.2.10 must show directly that the centre-modified data have fundamental Hodge embeddings, for instance through W = Hom_{Z_G}(V,V) as in [KP18, proof of Lemma 4.6.22] (E81); and in Proposition 7.2.16(2) Lemma 7.2.13 gives very goodness only for the smaller group G_1, so the extension to G′_i must be proved, which the printed argument does when every real place of F over 𝔭_i is noncompact (E84).
routes.reason: The existing integral reduction candidate is the shared owner of these Shimura models. This work supplies the all-abelian odd-prime foundation and corrected descent rather than proposing another Shimura roadmap.

ON PARAHORIC (G, µ)-DISPLAYS
MANUEL HOFF
Abstract. We develop tools to study spaces of p-divisible groups and Abelian varieties with additional
structure. More precisely, we extend the deﬁnition of parahoric (Dieudonn´e) (G, µ)-displays given by Pappas
to not necessarily p-torsionfree base rings and also introduce the notion of an (m, n)-truncated (G, µ)-display.
Then we study the deformation theory of Dieudonn´e (G, µ)-displays.
As an application we realize the EKOR stratiﬁcation of the special ﬁber of a Kisin-Pappas integral
Shimura variety of Hodge

ON A CONJECTURE OF PAPPAS AND RAPOPORT
PATRICK DANIELS, POL VAN HOFTEN, DONGRYUL KIM, AND MINGJIA ZHANG
Abstract. We prove a conjecture of Pappas and Rapoport about the existence
of “canonical” integral models of Shimura varieties of Hodge type with quasi-
parahoric level structure at a prime p. For these integral models, we moreover
show uniformization of isogeny classes by integral local Shimura varieties and
prove a conjecture of Kisin and Pappas on local model diagrams.

sourceIssues.printed: 'Let (H,Y) be a Shimura datum with H^ad a classical group. Recall ... that there is central isogeny H̃ → H^♯ (which depends also on Y if H has a factor of type D) such that (H,Y) is of abelian type if and only if H^der is a quotient of H^♯.'
sourceIssues.correction: Restrict 4.6.21 (KP18 p. 205) to Shimura data (H,Y) with (H^ad,Y^ad) of abelian type. H^♯ (KPZ26 §7.2.1, pp. 76–77) is defined only when every simple factor of H^ad satisfies Deligne's third condition: for type D, the noncompact real places are all D^R or all D^H. This can fail when H^ad is merely classical (such data are not of abelian type). It holds when (H^ad,Y^ad) is of abelian type [De79, 1.3.10, 2.3.10], and then (H,Y) is of abelian type iff H^der is a quotient of H^♯. KP18 uses H^♯ only in the proof of Lemma 4.6.22, where (G_2,X_2) is of abelian type.
sourceIssues.reason: Footnote 8 (p.77) says 'H may not satisfy the third condition above'. It is H (the adjoint factors), not H^♯, that may fail the condition, so the existing correction ('H^♯ need not satisfy the third defining condition') names the wrong object. The existing 'affects: a stated result' overstates the damage: no KP18 result is applied outside the abelian-type case, where the condition holds.

review.reason: Revised on re-reading; independent check: The revision is right and should replace the ledger text. (1) Quotation: the sentence is KP18's published text (Publ. Math. IHÉS 128, printed p. 205, 4.6.21), checked on the image. It is word for word the arXiv wording the first reading quotes, so 'printed' should cite p. 205 rather than 'arXiv version'. (2) Object: KPZ26 §7.2.1 (p. 76) defines H^♯ only for groups H satisfying three conditions. The third says that for type D the noncompact real places are all of type D^R or all of type D^H. Footnote 8 (p. 77) says 'H may not satisfy the third condition above'. So it is H (its adjoint simple factors) that may fail the condition, and then H^♯ is undefined. The ledger's 'H^♯ need not satisfy the third defining condition' names the wrong object. (3) Falsity: a type-D datum whose noncompact places mix D^R and D^H is not of abelian type, and the recalled construction gives it no H^♯. So 'there is a central isogeny H̃ → H^♯ such that (H,Y) is of abelian type iff H^der is a quotient of H^♯' is false as stated for general (H,Y) with H^ad classical. (4) Reach: the only occurrences of ♯ in KP18 are 4.6.21 and the proof of Lemma 4.6.22 (p. 206: 'By [20] 2.3.10, we may choose G so that G^der = ∏ Res_{F_i/Q} G′_i^♯'). There (G_2,X_2) is of abelian type, so the conditions hold ([De79, 1.3.10, 2.3.10], as KPZ26 p. 77 recalls). No KP18 proof or result uses the false generality, so 'affects: nothing' is right and the ledger's 'a stated result' overstates the damage. 'error' is the right kind: the paper states something false, and KPZ26 itself calls it 'incorrectly asserted'.
