review.reason: Revised on re-reading; independent check: Checked on the p. 35 image; the quotation is exact. (1) The 'Equivalently' is false in characteristic p. In the GL_2 Weyl module V((p,0)), take v_i = F^{(i)}v_0. Then E v_i = (p−i+1)v_{i−1}, so E v_1 = p·v_0 = 0, although (p−1,1) and (p,0) are weights and the weight spaces are lines. (2) the first reading's addition (i) is right. With the literal definition the 'In particular' symmetry fails too: E v_p = v_{p−1} ≠ 0 but F v_{p−1} = p·v_p = 0. So the proof of 4.2.10(1) needs the weight reading, and with that reading (1) is fine. (3) The last sentence of the proof of 4.2.10(2) is false under either reading. The left inclusion for V(ν), v ∈ V(ν)_{ν'} with X_αv ≠ 0, gives the bound only for the pair (ϖ, −ν'−α), with ϖ = −w_0ν. Transposing, that pair is one where X_α: H^0(ϖ)_{ϖ''} → H^0(ϖ)_{ϖ''+α} is nonzero, because V(ν)^* = H^0(ϖ), not V(ϖ). In H^0(p) = Sym^p, for example, E·y^p = p·xy^{p−1} = 0. (4) the first reading's addition (ii) is right. k_α, j_α and the weight-reading l_α do not depend on the characteristic. The printed proof is valid in characteristic 0, where V(ν)^* = V(−w_0ν) and, by sl_2-theory, X_α is nonzero between adjacent weights of an irreducible module. So k_α ≤ l_α, and k_α = j_α = l_α under the hypothesis of 4.2.13. Minuscule pairs are realised in every characteristic, so Theorem 4.2.3 stands. (5) Against the revision's last sentence, Proposition 4.2.10(2) itself also holds in characteristic p; only its proof needs repair. Let g = (1+εt^{⟨λ,α⟩−l}X_α)t^λ. For v ∈ V(ν)_{ν'}, g^{−1}v = t^{−⟨λ,ν'⟩}v − εt^{−l−⟨λ,ν'⟩}X_αv. The right inclusion of (4.2.7) is part of the definition of S^FM, and it gives l ≤ ⟨μ,ν⟩ − ⟨λ,ν'⟩ whenever X_α: V(ν)_{ν'} → V(ν)_{ν'+α} is nonzero. On an α-string of weights of V(ϖ), ⟨μ,ϖ⟩ − ⟨λ,ϖ'⟩ is affine in the position. So its minimum over the string is at the bottom pair if ⟨λ,α⟩ ≤ 0 and at the top pair if ⟨λ,α⟩ ≥ 0. Bottom pairs are realised in the Weyl module V(ϖ) (right inclusion), and top pairs in H^0(ϖ) (left inclusion). If p does not divide the string length s, this holds in any module: X_{−α}X_αv = s·v for a bottom vector v, and X_αX_{−α}w = s·w for a top vector w. In general it follows from the Weyl (resp. good) filtration of the restriction to the Levi subgroup of α (Donkin, Mathieu). An SL_2 Weyl module has E v_n = v_{n−1} at the bottom, and H^0(n) has E(x^{n−1}y) = x^n at the top. Checks: Γ^p(k^3) = V(pϖ_1) has E_{12}y^{(p)} = x y^{(p−1)} ≠ 0, while Sym^p has E_{12}y^p = 0. Hence l ≤ l_α in characteristic p. So the error breaks the proof of Proposition 4.2.10(2) and the unnumbered 'Equivalently' sentence. Every numbered statement stands, so the reach is 'the proof', not 'a stated result'. Reviewer's decision: the reach stays 'a stated result'. As printed, Proposition 4.2.10(2) is unproved in characteristic p; the repair the independent check proposes (both inclusions of (4.2.7), with the minimum on each α-string at its bottom or top pair) relies, when p divides the string length, on the Donkin–Mathieu theorem on good filtrations restricted to Levi subgroups, whose exact form was not checked here. If that repair holds, the reach drops to 'the proof'. Theorem 4.2.3 and the equalities k_α = j_α = l_α stand in every characteristic.

Note that (𝔖, E𝔖) is not a frame in the sense of §5.1, so its tilde module is taken to be φ*(F) ⊂ φ*(M_𝔖) directly. For an O_K-point the filtration lives over O_K, and the natural ideal over 𝔖 is E(x)𝔖. review.reason: Checked on the p. 61 image and against KP18 (Lem. 3.2.6, proof of Lem. 3.2.9). The first reading's diagnosis is right. The 𝔖-object the paper points to is KP18's F = L ⊕ E(x)T, the preimage of the O_K-filtration; KP18 Lem. 3.2.6 is exactly what puts s_a ⊗ 1 in F^⊗. F is a pair over the ideal E(x)𝔖. That is not a frame in the paper's sense (§5.1.1 requires φ = pφ_1 on I, but φ(E) ∉ p𝔖). So λ̄: 𝔖 → Ŵ(O_K) and x ↦ ε: 𝔖 → W[ε] are not strict morphisms of §5.1 frames: they are u-morphisms with u = V^{-1}(E([π_K])) and σ(a_0) respectively. So τ, (5.1.4) and Lemma 5.1.11 cannot be applied verbatim, and 'along the lines of Prop. 5.3.11 … somewhat simpler' hides this. One refinement to the first reading's reason: the connection isomorphism never has to be base-changed along a non-strict map. Only the strict maps (W[ε],(p)) → D_{k[ε]}, (W[ε],(p,ε)) → D_{k[ε]/k} and D_{R_G} → D_{k[ε]} carry c. What must be supplied is the identification of the tilde modules and tensors along the non-strict maps. The proof can be completed: for e(K/Ĕ) ≥ 2, O_K/((π_K²)+(π_E)) = k[ε] (for K = Ĕ there is nothing to prove). KP18 (3.2.10) gives φ*(F) ⊗ Ŵ(O_K) = M̃_{Ŵ(O_K),1}. The same computation with E(x) ↦ p(a_0 + a_1ε) gives φ*(F) ⊗ W[ε] = M̃_{W[ε],1}. The two resulting identifications over Ŵ(k[ε]) agree, because both rescale the T-part by V^{-1}(E([ε])) = σ(a_0). So Prop. 5.3.18 is true and the omission is expository. It is not trivial, however, given that the KP18 error concerned exactly this kind of construction. The paper says Prop. 5.3.18 is not used elsewhere.

sourceIssues.printed: Using the R-smoothness condition, by Proposition 2.1.5 (3), we see that the natural morphisms 𝒢 → 𝒢′, 𝒢̃ → 𝒢̃′, are closed immersions.
sourceIssues.correction: Either prove that R-smoothness of the centralizer of a maximal Q̆_p-split torus is preserved by the tame extension Q̃_p/Q_p, and then apply Proposition 2.1.5(3) over Q̃_p, or add this as a hypothesis of Theorem 6.1.1. A sufficient hypothesis is that this centralizer is built from quasi-tame tori by extensions, which covers the §7.2 applications.
sourceIssues.reason: Proposition 2.1.5(3) assumes R-smoothness of the source group over the base field of the building. Theorem 6.1.1 assumes R-smoothness of G over Q_p only. Over Q_p, applied with K̃ = Q̃_p, the proposition gives a closed immersion 𝒢 → Res 𝒢̃'. It does not give one for 𝒢̃ → 𝒢̃'. That closed immersion is needed for Res𝒢̃ ↪ Res𝒢̃' ↪ GL(Λ̃) in (6.1.4) and (6.1.6), hence for J ↪ GL(Λ̃) to be an integral Hodge embedding to which Proposition 5.3.11 and Corollary 5.3.4 apply. Case for the defence: the hypothesis probably does persist in practice. In the §7 applications, R-smoothness comes from quasi-tame tori and extensions (Proposition 2.1.5(1),(2), Lemma 7.2.11), and those are stable under tame base change. I could not settle the general case either way, so this is recorded as a gap, not an error.

review.reason: Checked on the p. 63 image. Proposition 2.1.5(3) (p. 10) takes G → G' over a base field K, a point x ∈ B(G,K) and an extension K̃. It assumes G is R-smooth over K and concludes 𝒢_x ↪ Res_{Õ/O}𝒢̃'_{x'}. With K = Q_p and K̃ = Q_p it gives 𝒢 → 𝒢'. For 𝒢̃ → 𝒢̃' over Z̃_p it has to be applied with K = Q̃_p, which requires G_{Q̃_p} to be R-smooth. Theorem 6.1.1 assumes R-smoothness over Q_p only. Neither this paper nor KZ25 §2.4 proves that R-smoothness survives a ramified tame base change: KZ25 §2.4.2 records only invariance under F → F̆. Tame descent of Néron models gives only the converse, that T_{Q̃_p} R-smooth implies T R-smooth. The missing input is essential. G^der = G'^der and T'_{Q̃_p} = ∏ Res_{F̃_i/Q̃_p}(split) is R-smooth. So 𝒯̃ → 𝒯̃' is a closed immersion exactly when T_{Q̃_p} is R-smooth, where T_{Q̃_p} is still the centralizer of a maximal Q̆̃_p-split torus. The step cannot be bypassed either. 𝒢 ↪ Res𝒢̃' does follow from 2.1.5(3) with K̃ = Q̃_p. But the proof applies Proposition 5.3.11 to 𝒥 = Res𝒢̃ ↪ GL(Λ̃) of (6.1.6), and then Corollary 5.3.4 via '𝒢 cut out in 𝒥 by endomorphisms'. Both need Res𝒢̃ → Res𝒢̃' to be a closed immersion. Case for the defence: tori built from quasi-tame tori by extensions (Proposition 2.1.5(1),(2)) stay in that class after tame base change. In §7.2, R-smoothness of G comes from that class: Z^c_G is quasi-tame (condition (4)), Lemma 7.2.5 and Lemma 7.2.11. The other uses of Theorem 6.1.1 are to GSp. So the applications I checked are covered, but the theorem as stated (general R-smoothness) is not proved. Gap, not error: I could not construct an R-smooth T with T_{Q̃_p} not R-smooth.

sourceIssues.printed: If we consider Λ̃^* as a Z̃_p-lattice in V ⊗_{Q_p} Q̃_p, then we have Λ̃^* = Λ̃^∨. Let L denote the lattice chain {(π̃^iΛ̃)^Γ}_{i∈Z} in V. Then L^∨ = {(π̃^iΛ̃^*)^Γ}_{i∈Z} and L ⊕ L^∨ = {(π̃^i(Λ̃ ⊕ Λ̃^*))^Γ}_{i∈Z}.
sourceIssues.correction: Replace Λ̃^* by the ψ-dual Λ̃^∨ throughout. The (i,γ)-component of Λ̃^∨ is γ(δ_{F_i/Q_p})D_{F̃_i/Q̃_p}^{-1}Λ̃_i^* = D_{Q̃_p/Q_p}D_{F̃_i/F_i}^{-1}Λ̃_i^*, which equals Λ̃_i^* only when D_{Q̃_p/Q_p}O_{F̃_i} = D_{F̃_i/F_i}, e.g. when Q̃_p/Q_p is unramified or every F_i/Q_p is unramified. Then L^∨ = {(π̃^iΛ̃^∨)^Γ}_{i∈Z} (by the identity ((π̃^mΛ̃)^Γ)^∨ = (π̃^{-m}δ^{-1}Λ̃^∨)^Γ) and L ⊕ L^∨ = {(π̃^i(Λ̃ ⊕ Λ̃^∨))^Γ}_{i∈Z}. Λ̃^∨ is a Γ-stable sum of Õ_i-lattices c_{i,γ}Λ̃_i^* with the same stabilizers, so the argument of Theorem 6.1.1 applies to Λ̃, Λ̃^∨ and Λ̃ ⊕ Λ̃^∨.
sourceIssues.reason: Counterexample. Take F_1 = Q_p, F_2 = Q_p(√p), W_1 = Q_p^2 and W_2 = F_2^2 with standard symplectic forms, H_i = GL_2, G the common-multiplier subgroup, and x hyperspecial. Then Q̃_p = Q_p(√p) satisfies every requirement of the proof, and F̃_2 = Q̃_p. With standard Λ̃_i one has Λ̃^* = Λ̃, but Λ̃^∨ = Z̃_p^2 ⊕ √pZ̃_p^2 ⊕ √pZ̃_p^2, since δ_{F_2/Q_p} ~ √p and D_{F̃_2/Q̃_p} = 1. The member (π̃Λ̃)^Γ = pZ_p^2 ⊕ √pO_{F_2}^2 of L has ψ-dual p^{-1}Z_p^2 ⊕ √p^{-1}O_{F_2}^2. That is not of the form (π̃^jΛ̃^*)^Γ = p^{⌈j/2⌉}Z_p^2 ⊕ √p^{j}O_{F_2}^2. It is (π̃^{-2}Λ̃^∨)^Γ, as the corrected formula predicts. Case for the defence: if Λ̃_i^* is read as the dual of Λ̃_i for the (i,γ)-component of ψ ⊗ Q̃_p, the claim is a tautology. But the text defines Λ̃_i^* as 'the ψ_i dual'. The δ-normalization of §6.1.8 makes ψ_i-duality agree with ψ-duality over Q_p, and that agreement is not preserved by the ramified base change to Q̃_p.

review.reason: Checked on the p. 66 image: 'let Λ̃_i^* denote the ψ_i dual of Λ̃_i', 'Λ̃^* := ⊕_i ⊕_{∈Γ/Γ_i} Λ̃_i^*', 'then we have Λ̃^* = Λ̃^∨', 'L^∨ = {(π̃^iΛ̃^*)^Γ}'. By §6.1.8, ∨ is the dual for the Q̃_p-bilinear extension of ψ = Σ_i Tr_{F_i/Q_p}(δ_{F_i/Q_p}^{-1}ψ_i). On the summand W_i ⊗_{F_i,γ} F̃_i of V ⊗ Q̃_p this form is Tr_{F̃_i/Q̃_p}(γ(δ_{F_i/Q_p})^{-1}ψ_i). So the (i,γ)-component of Λ̃^∨ is γ(δ_{F_i/Q_p})·D_{F̃_i/Q̃_p}^{-1}·Λ̃_i^*. By transitivity of differents this is D_{Q̃_p/Q_p}·D_{F̃_i/F_i}^{-1}·Λ̃_i^*. It equals Λ̃_i^* only when D_{Q̃_p/Q_p}O_{F̃_i} = D_{F̃_i/F_i}. In the tame case this means e(F̃_i/Q̃_p)(e(Q̃_p/Q_p)−1) = e(F̃_i/F_i)−1, which fails in general. If some F_i/Q_p is tamely ramified, Q̃_p has to contain that ramification, so the case cannot be avoided. I re-derived the first reading's example with p odd, Q̃_p = F_2 = Q_p(√p), π̃ = √p and |Γ| = 2. Then (π̃Λ̃)^Γ = pZ_p^2 ⊕ √pO_{F_2}^2. Its ψ-dual is p^{-1}Z_p^2 ⊕ √p^{-1}O_{F_2}^2, because O_{F_2}^2 is self-dual for Tr(δ^{-1}ψ_2). For every j, (π̃^jΛ̃^*)^Γ = p^{⌈j/2⌉}Z_p^2 ⊕ √p^jO_{F_2}^2, and none of these is that dual. The dual is (π̃^{-2}Λ̃^∨)^Γ. So the claimed L^∨ and L ⊕ L^∨ are false. The proof's own 'Indeed' sentence, read as the tame-descent identity ((π̃^mΛ̃)^Γ)^∨ = (π̃^{-m}δ^{-1}Λ̃^∨)^Γ with δ^{-1}Z̃_p = π̃^{1−e}Z̃_p, actually proves L^∨ = {(π̃^iΛ̃^∨)^Γ}. So the only false step is the identification Λ̃^* = Λ̃^∨. It is a false assertion about two different lattices whose invariant chains differ, not a slip of notation. The defence would read Λ̃_i^* as the dual for the (i,γ)-component of ψ ⊗ Q̃_p. That makes the claim a tautology, but it contradicts the printed definition 'ψ_i dual'. Repair: use Λ̃^∨. It is Γ-stable because ψ is defined over Q_p. Its components are F̃_i^×-multiples of Λ̃_i^*, so they have the same stabilizers in H_i ⊗ F̃_i. The argument of Theorem 6.1.1 therefore applies to Λ̃^∨ and Λ̃ ⊕ Λ̃^∨ unchanged, and the statement of Theorem 6.1.9 stands.

review.reason: Checked on the p. 66 image: '(π̃^{−m}δ^{−1}Λ̃^∨)^Γ is the ψ-dual of (π̃^{−m}δ^{−1}Λ̃)^Γ'. sourceIssues.correction: Prove directly that ρ_i extends to a very good (𝒢′_i, μ′_i) → (GL(ℒ), μ_d); 'Lemma 7.2.13 and Corollary 6.3.5' give this only for G_1 ⊊ G′_i. If μ′_i factors through G_1 (true when every real place of F inducing 𝔭_i is noncompact), the first reading's argument works. Since G′_i = G_1·Z_{G′_i} and the centre fixes the μ′_i-filtration, both groups have the same generic orbit, the same local model in Gr(d, tot ℒ′), the same R_G and the same M̃_1. Tensors cutting out 𝒢′_i are fixed by 𝒢_1 ⊂ 𝒢′_i, so they are horizontal by Lemma 5.2.3 once Corollary 6.3.5 gives very-goodness for 𝒢_1. Here ℒ′ must be 𝒢′_i-stable. If a compact place induces 𝔭_i, μ′_i has a component in (Res_{K/Q}G_m)^{Nm_{K/F}=1} and does not factor through G_1. Then an analogue of 6.3.4–6.3.5 is needed for the group generated by G_1 and that torus (compare the extra K^×-factor of 6.2.8 and Remark 6.2.9). Afterwards use Lemma 7.2.13, as in case (1), to pass from G′ to G.
sourceIssues.reason: G_1 is a proper subgroup of G′_i. Over F_i, K ⊗_F F_i = F_i × F_i and V_i = W ⊕ W, and the torus (Res_{K/Q}G_m)^{N_{K/F}=1} ⊂ Z_{G,0} ⊂ G′ acts by (y, y^{-1}) on the two copies. So Z_{G′_i} has dimension 3 (from F^×, K_S^1, K^1) while Z_{G_1} has dimension 2 (K^× × K^×). review.reason: Checked on p. 83 (same in arXiv v3). I recomputed the groups. Over F_i, K_S and K both split: H_{F_i} is an inner form of PGL, and K is split above p by choice. So V_i = W_i ⊗ (K ⊗_F F_i) has four isotypic blocks W^{±,(𝔓)} and W^{±,(𝔓̄)}. Z_{H′_i} contains three things: the scalars x; K_S^1, acting by y^{±1} on W^±; and K^1, acting by z^{±1} on the 𝔓- and 𝔓̄-copies. These characters are independent, so the centre is a 3-dimensional torus. By contrast, G_1 of 6.3.4 has centre K^× × K^× (a on V, b on V̄). So G_1 ⊊ G′_i: the paper itself claims only an inclusion here, whereas in case (1) it claims an isomorphism with 6.2.8's G_1, which I confirmed. Lemma 7.2.13 only descends from G′ to (G′ ∩ GSp)^0 with the same derived group. G_1 is not of that form, since G′_i ⊂ Res GSp(V_i,Ψ_i) by Lemma 7.2.8(2). Corollary 6.3.5 gives very-goodness only for 𝒢_1. So the step from 𝒢_1 to 𝒢′_i is missing, as the first reading says. The first reading's repair, and the paper's own sentence 'μ′_i factors through G_1', need one caveat. At an embedding φ of F_i that comes from a compact real place of F, the H^♯-part of h is trivial and h_T (T ↔ I_c, §7.2.3 and [KP18, Lem. 4.6.22]) makes μ_φ central: weight 1 on the 𝔓-copy of W_i and weight 0 on the 𝔓̄-copy. Any G_1 as in 6.3.4 with V_i|_{G_1} a sum of ρ_1 acts by a single scalar on all standard-type blocks W^{+,(𝔓)} and W^{+,(𝔓̄)}. So μ′_i then does not factor through G_1. In that case V_i|_{G′_i} is the sum of two non-isomorphic twists (by z and z^{-1}) of ρ_1, close to the situation of Remark 5.3.8. The missing step is short only when every real place inducing 𝔭_i is noncompact. Prop. 7.2.16 is still very plausibly true, so the kind is gap and the reach is the proof.

summaryBefore: A 203-item extraction of the complete published paper, separating normal integral local models, classical Schubert tangent geometry, corrected display connections, very-good embedding existence and all-abelian-type integral models at odd p. Eight unique ownership routes reuse the existing root/local-model/tensor/Shimura candidates and isolate genuinely additional integral representation,diamond and shtuka directions. Original prerequisite proof closure and several construction expansions remain explicit gaps; this is a partial checkpoint, not formalization.
